Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10032 at 14 FR 429 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 28, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 1, 1949 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 580 to 2224 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The list of carriers (Eastern, Western and Southeastern regions) follows the signature block in the held text; it identifies the carriers and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10032 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10032_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10032_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_cf5124cbbf.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated April 11, 1949 and a letter of transmittal to the President dated Washington, D.C., April 11, 1949; the board states that the President approved, on February 19, 1949, an extension permitting it to file its report not later than April 13, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking April 11, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on April 11, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to May 11, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President approved on February 19, 1949 an extension of the report time to not later than April 13, 1949; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

Executive Order 10044 (official Federal Register text, 14 FR 1227, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits Atomic Energy Commission employees, with the General Manager's approval, to hold office as constables, deputy sheriffs or other law enforcement officers and other state or local offices, subject to a non-interference determination. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

EO 12553 (reading record LSP-EO_12553, read once in full; the table row '10054 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations') revokes the order outright, with no effective-date wording; the claim therefore rests on the on_signing reading, 1986-02-25, and treats that date as an upper bound, not a certified end. Inventory: the dossier's single clause (chars 826-2170) covers the whole operative paragraph from 'By virtue of the authority' to the end of the proviso and the order has no other section; kept. Earlier-end tests. (1) Own terms: the order has no sunset or termination clause. The five-year period is a condition on when Gross's service must end to carry the reemployment right; it does not say the modification expires, and its start date (the unheld beginning of his service) is not needed to find an end because it is not an end. A window or report-type deadline is never an end. (2) Parent chain: Parent-order chain read in the held official texts: EO 9721 (11 FR 5209, May 10, 1946) para. 3(a) reemploys an employee whose international-organization service is 'terminated without prejudice within three years from the date of such transfer' and requires application within ninety days after termination; EO 9949 (13 FR 2089, 1948-04-17) gave the same five-year relief to Paul D. Miles; EO 10103 (1950-02-01) amends only secs. 1 and 2 of EO 9721 and does not touch para. 3(a) or name EO 10054; EO 10804 (24 FR 1147, signed 1959-02-12) sec. 2 revokes EO 9721, EO 10103 and EO 10774 'except that each shall be considered to remain in effect' for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (72 Stat. 961) who do not elect its coverage 'and for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order' before that date; EO 11138 (1964-01-07, Frederick Strauss) and EO 11303 (1966-09-12, Reginald C. Price) waive limits in EO 9721 for other named persons. EO 10804 names neither EO 10054, EO 9949 nor EO 10415, revokes only the parent, and expressly keeps rights vested under it; because Gross's window had closed by 1954-04-29 at the latest, nothing but already vested rights could remain under the modification in 1959, so the 1959 partial revocation of the parent neither ends nor changes this clause and is ruled out as an earlier end (it is not attachable as a structured later event because the dossier holds no ACT record for it; the held official text was read). EO 11138 and EO 11303 name other persons and EO 10103 does not touch para. 3(a), so all three are ruled out. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

The held page also prints neighbouring documents, which are outside the inventory. Text and inventory: an enacting paragraph amending Executive Order 9721 and two numbered amendments, recorded as three clauses. Amendment 1 adds to section 1 of Executive Order 9721, effective as of May 10, 1946, a sentence beginning "Any employee so transferred shall, for a period not to exceed three years from the date of transfer", which treats a transferred employee as on leave of absence from federal employment while employed by the organization, provided he is later reemployed under section 3. Amendment 2 revives section 2 of Executive Order 9721, which had become inoperative on May 10, 1949, effective as of that date, and restates it: it gives competitive status to certain transferred war-service indefinite employees, and treats employees serving in an organization on September 30, 1949 as in active-duty status on that date for the purposes of Executive Order No. 10080. Partial revocation in 1959: section 2 of Executive Order 10804, signed February 12, 1959 and printed at 24 FR 1147 in the Federal Register of February 14, 1959 (held govinfo text layer), lists Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950, and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, the last "insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic" Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957; the singular qualifier attaches to Executive Order 10774 alone. All three are revoked, except that "each shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any" employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and does not elect coverage under section 6 of that Act, and "for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order prior to the date of the enactment of the" Act. Executive Order 10103 was therefore revoked generally in 1959 but remained in effect for those two saved classes. Later presidential orders applied it as still in effect for saved employees: Executive Order 11138, signed January 7, 1964 (29 FR 225), and Executive Order 11303 (31 FR 11963, filed September 12, 1966) each modify Executive Order 9721 as amended by Executive Order 10103 by waiving the section 1 leave-of-absence limit for one named employee. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. The table also lists 9721. That revocation, without exception, is the first end of the saved remainder and so of the whole order. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Texas & Pacific Railway Company and its subsidiaries, including the Fort Worth Belt Railway Company and the Texas Pacific-Missouri Pacific Terminal Railroad of New Orleans, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Texas & Pacific Railway Company or its subsidiaries, including the Fort Worth Belt Railway Company and the Texas Pacific-Missouri Pacific Terminal Railroad of New Orleans, or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Executive Order 10129 (15 FR 3499 (Federal Register of June 6, 1950)) was signed June 3, 1950. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date; the text breaks across a page after paragraph 7 and resumes on a later page of the same issue, so paragraph 7 appears in two pieces. It creates the President's Commission on Migratory Labor (paragraph 1), directs it to inquire into five subjects (paragraph 2), requires a written report by December 15, 1950 (paragraph 3), authorizes hearings (paragraph 4), directs consultation with the Department of State (paragraph 5), directs agency cooperation (paragraph 6), provides funding for the fiscal years 1950 and 1951 from the Emergency Fund for the President (paragraph 7) and provides in paragraph 8 that the Commission ceases to exist thirty days after its report unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated on May 31, 1951, the day the Commission ceased to exist. Executive Order 10192 (15 FR 9029 (Federal Register of December 19, 1950)), signed December 15, 1950, amended paragraph 3 (the report date becomes March 1, 1951) and paragraph 8 (“Thirty days” becomes “Sixty days”). Executive Order 10236 (16 FR 3607 (Federal Register of April 27, 1951)), signed April 26, 1951, amended paragraph 8 as amended to read “The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951.”, which fixes the end. The report date of paragraph 3 and the report-relative cessation of paragraph 8 are not ends: the held corpus does not give the date the report was rendered, and Executive Order 10236 replaced the report-relative rule with a fixed date while the Commission still existed. Executive Order 10193's Federal Register page contains the text of Executive Order 10192 and cites Executive Order 10129 only for that reason; it is not a separate amendment. The held-text search for citations of the order found only Executive Orders 10192, 10236 and their page copies. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists two hits (the 10192 and 10236 amendments); the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit.

EO 10134 (June 28, 1950) further extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1950 to June 30, 1954. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1954-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date of this order", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10138 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Executive Order 10215 (16 FR 1703 (Federal Register of February 20, 1951)) was signed February 16, 1951. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only operative command exempts Arthur A. Quinn, Comptroller of Customs with headquarters at New York, New York, from compulsory retirement for age under the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, “for an indefinite period of time, not extending beyond June 30, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated: by its own words the exemption cannot extend beyond June 30, 1951. The period is described as indefinite but capped, so the cap is the latest date on which the exemption could be in force. No held source shows that the exemption lapsed earlier (for example by Mr. Quinn's separation from office), and none shows any extension: the person-name search of the held order texts found no other order naming him, and the held-text search for the order's number found no citation. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10449 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board record (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10449_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10449_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_890e74e86f.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a National Mediation Board record for Emergency Board No. 104 stating that no members were appointed and that the parties reached agreement on April 26, 1953, so that no emergency board was set up for hearing the dispute; there is no report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on EO 10449 (a board never constituted is treated like the other emergency-board orders) the order stayed on the books until its express revocation; the fact that the board was never constituted is disclosed here, and the agreement of the parties on April 26, 1953 (a statement in that record) is a spent fact and not an end. The thirty-day report deadline (to May 24, 1953 on the inclusive reading) is a deadline and not an end. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Section 2 begins on page 2397 and continues on page 2399 after the issue's contents pages; the clause is quoted from page 2399. Operative clauses: the Administrator's recommendation of volunteer Federal personnel for State and local pre-emergency civil-defense training (sec. 1); the agency head's year-to-year authorization (sec. 2) and its three conditions (sec. 2(a)-(c)); continued pay, status and travel (sec. 3); a construction rule (sec. 4); and two definitions (sec. 5). There is no expiry, condition or report duty. Later events, read in the held texts: EO 10773 (July 1, 1958), EO 10782 (effective August 26, 1958, renaming the office in EO 10773's substituted references) and EO 11051 section 603(d) (September 27, 1962) only substituted the responsible officials (ODCM/OCDM Director, then OEP Director or Secretary of Defense); they are amendments, not ends. Section 1's reference to section 3 of EO 10346 describes the arrangements the recommendations serve; EO 10346 was revoked by EO 11490 in 1969, but section 1 does not make its own authority depend on EO 10346, and EO 10529 was still being maintained by amendment, so that revocation is not treated as an end. EO 10541 (June 30, 1954) further extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1954 to June 30, 1958. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1958-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 10559 (Sept. 8, 1954; 19 FR 5879) has two operative sections: sec. 1 delegates to the Budget Director the President's authority to allocate the 'Expenses of Management Improvement' appropriation (and any reenactment); sec. 2 requires reports and direction of the funded activities. Neither section has an expiry or condition; the delegation follows the paragraph as reenacted, and EO 11230 sec. 1(23) itself delegates the paragraph as reenacted in the Executive Office Appropriation Act 1965, so the authority was still live in 1965. No amendment of EO 10559 is recorded in the OFR catalog edges or the 1989 Codification disposition table ('Superseded by EO 11230'). EO 11230 sec. 2(2) expressly supersedes EO 10559; EO 11230 states no effective date and so took effect on issuance, June 28, 1965. Both clauses therefore first ended on 1965-06-28, which is also the whole-order end. Savings: EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps prior actions and regulations in effect under EO 11230 and sec. 3(b) redirects references; the function itself passes to EO 11230 sec. 1(23). No current-law citation of EO 10559 was found (U.S. Code release 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14).

EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps in effect all actions taken and regulations prescribed or approved in the matters covered by its sec. 1 (which re-delegates the same presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget) until amended or revoked under EO 11230; sec. 3(b) redirects references to superseded orders to the corresponding provision of EO 11230. The functions therefore pass to EO 11230 and past actions survive under it; nothing continues to rest on this order. EO 11230 sec. 1(23) re-delegates the same management-improvement allocation authority (as reenacted) and the same reporting and direction duty.

EO 10589 (January 15, 1955) appointed or continued Charles S. Kelly (chairman), Ernest C. Oberholtzer and Paul Clement as members, amended EO 6783 accordingly, and provided that the two designated members continue to be designated by and serve at the pleasure of the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. The amendment and the designated-member rule had no term of their own and ceased with the committee on June 30, 1966 (EO 11031 sec. 2(b) restated the same rule in 1962 without ending it). The appointment was a one-time act completed on issuance; EO 11031 sec. 2(a) re-appointed the same members for a fixed term ending June 30, 1966. Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10879 (25 FR 4893, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of June 3, 1960; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10879.txt), headed Executive Order 10879, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 1, 1960. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Establishing the White House Service Certificate and the White House Service Badge). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: five numbered paragraphs, which the dossier lists as five clauses, and the badge design that paragraph 3 makes part of the order (a figure, not a clause); I confirm the inventory is complete. Paragraph 1 establishes the White House Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Air Force, other than Presidential Aides, detailed to White House duty for at least one year after January 20, 1953. Paragraph 2 provides for the certificate's design and for award by the service Secretaries on recommendation of the Presidential Aides. Paragraph 3 establishes the White House Service Badge, which may be worn during the detail. Paragraph 4 limits each person to one certificate. Paragraph 5 allows posthumous award of the certificate. First end: Executive Order 12793, signed March 20, 1992 (57 FR 10281, Federal Register of March 25, 1992), section 5 of which states that it supersedes Executive Order 10879 of June 1, 1960, as amended; it names this order and ends every paragraph. It has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed. Later events before the end: Executive Order 11174 (September 1, 1964) amended all five numbered paragraphs by restating them; Executive Order 11407 (April 23, 1968) restated paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of Executive Order 11174; and Executive Order 11520 (March 25, 1970) restated paragraphs 1 and 3 of Executive Order 11407. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, so these are later events and not ends; because the 1964 restatement replaced the whole text of every paragraph and the later orders replaced more of paragraphs 1 to 3, the substance of the clauses changed and a human reviewer should read the before and after wording. The dossier's leads for Executive Orders 11407 and 11520 (target provision not located) are resolved by reading their held texts; the current-law lead without an original-source hash is not used. Searches: the three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order and the later-events search returned the hits recorded here as Executive Orders 11174 and 12793. Executive Order 12793 continues a certificate and badge under the Presidential Service names, but it does so by its own sections 1 and 2 and supersedes this order, so it ends this order and does not extend it.

EO 10880 (June 7, 1960; 25 FR 5131, held official FR scan text) allowed indefinite and temporary employees meeting stated service conditions to have their appointments converted to career or career-conditional appointments. Six operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Sec. 1(a) with its conditions (i)-(v), Sec. 1(b) postal substitutes, Sec. 2 definitions, Sec. 3 returning service members, Sec. 4 exclusions, Sec. 5 rule-making). The order's own terms close the agency-recommendation window for Sec. 1(a) one year after its date, but set no date by which conversions had to be completed (Sec. 1(b) conversions wait for career substitute vacancies), and Sec. 3 stays open for any qualifying service member re-employed after discharge; no earlier cessation can therefore be proved from the order itself, and the recommendation deadline is not treated as an end. EO 12107 (effective January 1, 1979) redesignated the Civil Service Commission as the Office of Personnel Management in this order, confirming it was still treated as in force. EO 12608 of September 9, 1987, Sec. 1, revoked it (no separate effective date), which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end; the same section preserves 'benefits already conferred'. USC note at 5 U.S.C. 3301 and the OFR 1989 table agree.

EO 12608 Sec. 1 expressly provides that, notwithstanding the revocation of EO 10880, benefits already conferred under it before revocation shall not be affected: appointments already converted to career or career-conditional status stand. No new conversion could be made under the order after September 9, 1987.

EO 10889 (Oct. 5, 1960; 25 FR 9633) adds paragraphs (p), (q) and (r) to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 and, in sec. 2, supersedes four 1960 presidential letters under Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 45(a). Clause by clause: (p)(1), the determination power under sec. 45(a), ran until EO 11164 substituted the whole of paragraph (p) on Aug. 1, 1964 (EO 11164 states no effective date; effective on issuance). (p)(2), the conveyance power, was delegated only 'until July 1, 1964' by this order's own words, so it first ended on 1964-07-01 by its own terms, before EO 11164 restored a conveyance power without that limit. (q) was replaced in full by EO 10960 on Aug. 21, 1961 (substitution 'to read as follows', effective on issuance). Sec. 2's supersession of the four letters was completed on issuance, Oct. 5, 1960 (spent; recorded as its first end). (r) and the enacting words continued until EO 11230 sec. 2 superseded Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10889 (item 7), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. Convention: a clause whose whole text is replaced by a later order's substituted text ends on that order's effective date; the substituted text is the later order's clause. EO 10898 (December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, read in the held govinfo scan) established the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board of cabinet officers (sec. 1), gave it coordinating and study functions (sec. 2), provided agency assistance (sec. 3), made it advisory only (sec. 4) and required reports (sec. 5). It has no term of its own. Earlier clause-level ends: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962) substituted a new sec. 1(b), so the original membership list ended then; EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) struck all of sec. 1(b) as amended and changed the quorum in sec. 1(d) from three to four, so the original quorum rule ended then. EO 11382 sec. 16(3) also revoked EO 10858, which sec. 4 cites for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety; this is recorded as a later event on sec. 4, but the section's main rule (Board advisory only) continued. EO 11515 (March 13, 1970) terminated the Board and revoked EO 10898 and EO 10986 without a stated effective date, so the remaining clauses ended on March 13, 1970, the whole-order end. The Board consisted of federal officials and ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies.

EO 11515 sec. 6 provides that 'such actions as may be necessary to wind up any outstanding affairs of the bodies terminated by this order shall be carried out by the Bureau of the Budget' or agencies its Director designates. The Board's residual affairs were thus transferred for winding up only; no function, right or obligation of the Board was continued. EO 10898 itself has no savings provision, and sec. 4 made the Board advisory, without control over any agency, so no agency action depended on it.

EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. Under the section of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 that the order cites (printed as section 6130(a), with the parenthetical citation 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)), it orders that any income, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1956 to 1963, inclusive, shall, during the Eighty-eighth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Public Works, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof, in connection with its investigation of the policies, procedures and practices involved in the administration of the Federal-Aid Highway Program, pursuant to House Resolution 56 of the 88th Congress, agreed to January 31, 1963; the inspection is to follow the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decision 6132; and the order takes effect on filing for publication in the Federal Register. First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Eighty-eighth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1963 to January 3, 1965. EO 11126 (November 1, 1963; 28 FR 11717-11718, read in the held govinfo scan) set up an Interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women of cabinet officers (Part I) and a Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women (Part II), with support provisions (Part III). It has no term of its own. Clause-level history: EO 11221 (May 6, 1965) substituted new texts for secs. 101(a), 103 and 201, so the original texts ended then. The Council was an advisory committee in existence on January 5, 1973 and would have expired under sec. 14(a)(1) of the Federal Advisory Committee Act on January 5, 1975, but EO 11827 (signed January 4, 1975) continued it to January 5, 1977 and EO 11948 (effective December 31, 1976) to December 31, 1978, so there was no statutory lapse. EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Council and revoked sec. 102(5) and Part II and rewrote sec. 103 and the second sentence of sec. 301, so those clauses ended then. The Committee clauses (federal officials, outside the Act) continued until EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11126 as amended, signed April 4, 1978 with no other effective date stated: that is the whole-order end. None of these orders contains a savings clause.

EO 12050 sec. 8 revokes EO 11126 'as amended' with no savings, transition or winding-up clause, and EO 12007 had already terminated the Citizens' Advisory Council without one. EO 11126 created advisory and coordinating bodies only: no right, benefit, office or obligation of a person depended on it. The National Advisory Committee for Women and the Interdepartmental Task Force that EO 12050 created rest on EO 12050 itself (policy continuity, not a survival of EO 11126).

Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 12079) prints Executive Order 11127 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1963-11-09; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. EO 11133 (December 17, 1963, signed by the President as printed at 28 FR 13835), read in full in the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11133.txt (machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, graded original_representation_unverified and counted as an official original; I did not inspect the PDF page images). Identity: the number, subject and date in the held text agree with the census register. Content: a single operative paragraph. Under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, it orders that any income, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1959 to 1963, inclusive, shall, during the Eighty-eighth Congress, be open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof, in connection with its study and investigation with respect to any financial or business interests or activities of any officer or employee or former officer or employee of the Senate, pursuant to Senate Resolution 212 of the 88th Congress, agreed to October 10, 1963; the inspection is to follow the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decision 6132; and the order takes effect on filing for publication in the Federal Register. First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Eighty-eighth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1963 to January 3, 1965. EO 11152 sec. 4 left all statutory functions (including the Secretary of Labor's under the Manpower Development and Training Act) where the law placed them, so nothing depended on the Committee's existence.

First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Eighty-ninth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1965 to January 3, 1967. The end is recorded as 1967-01-03, the last day of the Congress, inclusive; the alternative reading is that the Congress ends at noon on that day. The held Wayback capture of the House Historian page Session Dates of Congress, 80th to 89th Congresses (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11065_87th_Congress_term_dates_1961-01-03_to_1963-01-03_and_U.S._Const._amend._XX_sec._1_fo_1629d9be9b.txt; SHA-256 of the downloaded file ae41559e675086cd43b8f55648a5021e8fe6a9c48d2ec1990987ea933aa458e5) gives October 22, 1966 as the adjournment date of the last session of the 89th Congress; the adjournment of a session is not the end of the Congress, and it is disclosed as an earlier candidate that is not relied on. Its operative content is one adjusting sentence with four rate tables and three footnote rules (service-chief special rate, the O-1 to O-3 scope rule, senior enlisted adviser special rate); the sentence and footnotes are quoted verbatim, the table figures are cited by page because the OCR scatters them. The order had no expiry, but its rates were the ones next adjusted: EO 11475 adjusted the same rates for every grade, with new footnote rates, 'effective on July 1, 1969'. From that date the 1968 rates no longer governed pay, so every clause first ends on July 1, 1969 (implied supersession by the later adjustment), the whole-order end. EO 11812 Sec. 5(1) later superseded EO 11414 expressly, effective October 1, 1974 (Sec. 6); that cleanup supersession is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. The OFR 1989 table ('Superseded by EO 11812') and the 37 U.S.C. 203 note list it among the pre-1974 pay orders.

The order's rates were replaced prospectively; pay earned at those rates for service before the replacement date remained payable as accrued entitlements (including retroactive differences). No provision of the order, of the order that replaced its rates (EO 11475) or of EO 11812 continues any of its rates or rules after that date, and none of them contains a savings clause.

EO 11534 (June 4, 1970; 35 FR 8865, read in the held govinfo scan) created a National Council on Organized Crime of eighteen named federal officials to formulate a national strategy against organized crime. It has no term, report deadline or condition, and no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead). EO 12110 sec. 1-103(c) lists it among orders 'that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed'. That recital gives no date and is not itself a legal act ending the Council earlier; the order's own terms set no end, and the Council, composed wholly of full-time federal officers, was outside the termination rule of sec. 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (the continuance orders EO 11827 and EO 11948 accordingly do not list it). The legal first end of every clause is therefore the revocation, effective December 31, 1978 under sec. 1-105. Changes in some members' offices (for example the Post Office Department and the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs were later reorganized) altered who sat on the Council but did not end it; they were not separately researched.

EO 12110 revokes EO 11534 with no savings or winding-up clause. EO 11534 only created a coordinating council of federal officials charged with formulating a strategy; it conferred no right, benefit, office or obligation on any person, and the members' own statutory law-enforcement functions never depended on it. Nothing of the order was found to survive.

EO 11809 (September 30, 1974; 39 FR 35565) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 15, heading to FR Doc. 74-23127). Its five operative sections establish the President's Labor-Management Committee (eight labor, eight management members and a neutral coordinator), state its study-and-advice functions, direct it to encourage sector labor-management committees, direct agency cooperation and assign FACA functions to the Treasury. EO 11948 (held) section 4(a)(2) revokes it, effective December 31, 1976 under section 5. Because the Committee was created after January 5, 1973 and is absent from EO 11827's list of continued post-1973 committees, it may have terminated under the FACA two-year rule about three months before the formal revocation; the first ends are therefore left open rather than taken from the revocation. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; see EO 11849) and the 1989 OFR Codification table (revoked by EO 11948) agree on the formal history.

Clause inventory is complete and quoted from the official FR scan (the draft had none). EO 11832 (January 9, 1975; 40 FR 2415-2417, read in the held govinfo scan) established the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 (secs. 1-3) and an interdepartmental task force (sec. 4). Exact clause-level ends found: EO 11889 (November 25, 1975) replaced the original sec. 2(h), which had ended the Commission's work with 1975; EO 11979 (March 28, 1977) replaced the original sec. 1(b) membership rule (further amended by EO 11980). The other clauses are certainly terminated by the cutoff, since EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11832 as amended on April 4, 1978, but that revocation may be a clean-up. Under EO 11889 the Commission was to end after a final report due within thirty days after June 30, 1976. EO 11979 shows it was still operating in 1977 'in accord with Section 2' of Public Law 94-167, which directed it to organize the National Women's Conference, and the Commission was set up after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so sec. 14(a)(2) of that Act also bears on its duration. Without reading Public Law 94-167, which states how long the Commission lasted and when it ended, the first ends of the Commission and task-force clauses, the whole-order end and the savings question cannot be fixed honestly; they are left open.

I read the whole order: it amends the parent by adding at the end of Part III a new section 306, in which paragraph (a) states "there is hereby established a Development Coordination Committee", paragraph (b) allows consultation with other agencies, and later paragraphs give the Committee advisory and coordination functions. Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. Section 306 existed only inside the parent, so it ended with the parent on 1979-10-01.

EO 11861 of May 21, 1975 (40 FR 22531) placed a new complete list of positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule and in sec. 4 superseded 'Executive Order No. 11768 of February 20, 1974, as amended'; it states no effective date for itself (the only dates in it are the June 1, 1975 termination of one listed position), so it took effect on signing. The amending orders EOs 11774 (March 26, 1974), 11780 (April 22, 1974), 11831 (January 9, 1975) and 11843 (March 18, 1975, effective March 1, 1975) operated only as text inserted into EO 11768, so the supersession of EO 11768 'as amended' ended them too, except where an amendment had already been displaced. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11861') and the OFR catalog notes were used as leads only; every date comes from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). The supersession on May 21, 1975 came before the paragraph's own June 1, 1975 termination date, so the paragraph ended on May 21, 1975 (EO 11861 sec. 1(13) placed the same position anew, again to terminate June 1, 1975, under its own authority). Whole-order end: 1975-05-21.

EO 11861 sec. 3 protects, under EO 11861 itself, incumbents of the positions it lists from termination or reappointment; it does not keep any placement made by this order in force. No savings clause in this order or in EO 11861 preserves a provision of this order; level placements under 5 U.S.C. 5317 after May 21, 1975 rest on EO 11861 and later orders.

EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', which signals an earlier end. The likely earlier end is the two-year limit of Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(2), since the general continuance order of December 1976 (EO 11948) did not renew it. Because the Act's application and the absence of any other renewal are not proven from held sources, first ends and the whole-order end are left open. Savings: none found. The U.S. Code note (29 U.S.C. 171 note) and the eCFR hits are historical and report the revocation; no CONFLICT is open.

EO 12110 revokes EO 11849 with no savings or winding-up clause. EO 11849 created a labor-management committee that facilitated bargaining and made recommendations; it conferred no right, benefit or obligation on any person and gave the Committee no binding power, so nothing was found that could survive its end, whenever that end occurred.

EO 11861 (signed 1975-05-21, 40 FR 22531-22532), read in full from the held FR text, places 13 offices and positions in level IV (sec. 1) and 12 in level V (sec. 2) of the Executive Schedule, preserves incumbents' appointments (sec. 3) and supersedes EO 11768 (sec. 4). The machine own-term hits are all one sentence, item 1(13): 'to terminate effective June 1, 1975', the only dated own-term end in the order; it is addressed in the item (13) clause. EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18, 43 FR 37161-37162, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_12076) sec. 1-202 revokes the order 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing. Seventeen orders amended EO 11861 before that and were all read in full (EO 11864, 11872, 11877, 11885, 11893, 11898, 11908, 11927, 11976, 11983, 11986, 11995, 11999, 12025, 12035, 12060, 12069); a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts (whitespace and hyphenation normalised) finds EO 11861 named in those seventeen and in EO 12076 only, and the OFR catalog edges name the same set. The amendments delete, replace or move individual items, so those items have an earlier first end than the revocation: 1(1) on 1977-05-04 (EO 11983), 1(2) on 1975-09-02 (EO 11877), 1(6) and 1(7) on 1977-05-20 (EO 11986), 1(9) on 1978-06-30 (EO 12069), 1(10) on 1978-05-15 (EO 12060), 1(11) on 1977-05-04 (EO 11983), 1(12) on 1977-12-01 (EO 12025), 1(13) on 1975-08-01 by its own term as extended (EO 11864; see the clause and the conflict resolution for the EO 11877 re-placement), 2(1) on 1975-10-15 (EO 11885), 2(7) on 1975-09-02 (EO 11877) and 2(9) on 1975-12-31 (EO 11893). The other items, the two section leads and secs. 3 and 4 end with the revocation. Items added by amendment (positions 1(14)-(18), 2(7), 2(8), 2(9), 2(13)-(15) and new item 1(6)) are not clauses of the order as issued; they are recorded in the later events of the section leads. EO 11983 sec. 2 revoked EO 11872 and EO 12060 sec. 3 revoked EO 11995, both amending orders. EO 12076 re-lists positions and protects incumbents (sec. 1-201), which is why the savings state is transferred_or_accrued. Inventory: the dossier's 29 clauses cover Sec. 1 through Sec. 4; three spans were trimmed (see inventory_overrides).

Reading record LSP-EO_12076 (EO 12076, 43 FR 37161-37162, read once in full): sec. 1-101 and 1-102 place 17 positions in level IV and 14 positions in level V of the Executive Schedule, re-listing a large part of what EO 11861 placed (for example the HCFA Administrator, the Director of the Secret Service, the Associate Directors of OMB, the Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs, the PBGC Executive Director, the Commissioner on Aging); sec. 1-201 provides that nothing in the order terminates or affects the appointment, or requires the reappointment, of any occupant of a listed position who held it immediately before the order; sec. 1-202 revokes EO 11861, as amended. Its recital says it is made 'to codify other positions presently placed in levels IV and V'. Own-residual check, reading EO 11861 in full: it placed positions in the Executive Schedule, preserved incumbents' appointments (sec. 3) and superseded EO 11768 (sec. 4). The placements are carried forward by EO 12076, the incumbents' appointments are protected by sec. 3 of EO 11861 and sec. 1-201 of EO 12076, and the supersession of EO 11768 was complete when made and is not undone. The S4 prefill ('review') and its two STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS conflicts are resolved as transferred_or_accrued. EO 11864 (June 13, 1975; 40 FR 25579) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 11, complete from heading to FR Doc. 75-15839 and footnote). It is a single amending sentence: effective June 1, 1975, section 1 of EO 11861 (placing positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule) is revised at paragraph (13) to read 'Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury, to terminate effective August 1, 1975' (the OCR renders the closing '1975.”' with its footnote mark as '1,197571'; EO 11877 section 1(b), held, quotes the same paragraph with the date as 'August 1, 1975'). The order therefore fixed its own end: the placement lapsed on August 1, 1975, and that is the first end of the only clause and the whole-order end. The formal supersession came a month later: EO 11877 (September 2, 1975; 40 FR 40797, held), which states no effective date, superseded EO 11864 (section 2) and replaced paragraph (13) with an open-ended placement (section 1(b)); it is recorded as a later event, not as the first end, following the rule that a formal supersession can follow an earlier cessation under the order's own terms. A current-law note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 and the OFR catalog describe the same history (the note says the paragraph was 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975' and was superseded by EO 11877); the 1989 OFR Codification table lists EO 11864 as amending EO 11861 and superseded by EO 11877. The machine current-law hits for this order are that historical note, not a continuing basis.

EO 11864 has one operative provision: effective June 1, 1975 it revised paragraph (13) of section 1 of EO 11861 to place the Treasury Adviser (Counselor, Economic Policy Board) in level IV of the Executive Schedule, 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975'. The placement lapsed by its own terms on that date. EO 11868 (signed 1975-06-19, 40 FR 26255-26256), read in full from the held FR text, establishes the President's Commission on Olympic Sports (sec. 1), fixes its membership (sec. 2), directs a study of the United States Olympic Committee, impediments to fielding the best amateur athletes, financial support and related matters (sec. 3), requires two reports through the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (sec. 4), lets the Chairman set up advisory committees (sec. 5), provides Health, Education, and Welfare support and funds (sec. 6), member pay and travel (sec. 7) and the FACA assignment (sec. 8). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause: the first report is due 'within five months after the Commission meets for the first time' and the second, as replaced by EO 11936, 'no later than January 15, 1977'; both are report deadlines and, under the project rule, never an end. EO 11873 (1975-07-21) replaces sec. 2 in full and EO 11936 (1976-09-08) replaces sec. 4(c) in full, each on signing; the original wording of those two clauses first ends on those dates and the replacement text runs to the revocation. EO 11948 sec. 3 revokes 'Executive Order No. 11868, as amended' 'effective January 16, 1977', the whole order and without qualifier, one day after the replacement report date; the twelve other original clauses first end on 1977-01-16 and the whole-order end is the latest first end, 1977-01-16. Checked and ruled out: no other held order names EO 11868; EO 11948 sec. 4(b) supersedes EO 11827, not this order; the dossier's STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS conflict is resolved for 1977-01-16; no FACA two-year termination applies because the order was revoked 1977-01-16 and a FACA committee created 1975-06-19 could run to 1977-06-19. Inventory: the recitals and the issuing paragraph were added to the dossier's fourteen operative clauses; trailing page furniture (sec. 3(c)) and the editorial note after sec. 8 were cut. A prior pilot decision for this order (research/production/claim-kit-pilot-2026-10-18/producer-11948) reached the same replacement-and-revocation reading; it was read as a lead only and the texts were re-read. Limitations: the dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (only chain.generic_refs_excluded 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the actual submission dates of the two reports and any earlier winding-up of the Commission are not known and are not asserted.

EO 11958 (signed 1977-01-18, 42 FR 4311-4313), read in full from the held FR text, delegates the President's Arms Export Control Act functions to the Secretaries of State, Defense, the Treasury and Commerce (sec. 1(a)-(n)), sets coordination (sec. 2), allocates funds to the Secretary of Defense (sec. 3) and revokes EO 11501, with a savings proviso for actions taken under it (sec. 4). The machine own-term kinds are conditions (concurrence requirements in sec. 1(l)) and the 'until_event' wording of the sec. 4 proviso for EO 11501, none of which is an end of EO 11958; the order has no sunset or termination clause. EO 13637 (signed 2013-03-08, 78 FR 16129-16132, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_13637) sec. 4 revokes it 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing; the dossier's effective-date class 'unknown' is resolved from the text. Thirteen orders amended EO 11958 before that (EO 12118, 12163, 12210, 12321, 12365, 12423, 12560, 12680, 12738, 13030, 13091, 13118, 13284); the sections of each that amend EO 11958 were read in the held FR texts (several of these are omnibus orders whose other sections concern other orders and were not otherwise relied on); they are the only orders found by a by-number scan (whitespace and hyphenation normalised, which is needed because the held text of EO 12680 prints the number as '119 58') of all 6,652 held FR-original texts apart from EO 13637. They rewrite or extend individual delegations and re-letter the list but delete none, so every clause stays in force, as amended, until the revocation; the amendments are attached as later events on the clauses they change. The relettering by EO 13030 and EO 13091 moved the Section 42 delegation from subsection (n) to (o) and then (p). Inventory correction: the dossier's 18 clauses merge items (f)-(h) and (i)-(j) and fold sec. 4 into sec. 3 (see inventory_overrides; 22 clauses, no gap or overlap).

Reading record LSP-EO_13637 (EO 13637, 78 FR 16129-16132, read once in full): sec. 1 re-delegates the Arms Export Control Act functions (21 delegations, (a)-(u)) to the Secretaries of State and Defense and the Attorney General, so the functions that EO 11958 sec. 1 delegated are re-made, not abandoned; sec. 3 re-allocates funds to the Secretary of Defense; sec. 4 revokes EO 11958, as amended, 'except that, to the extent consistent with this order, all determinations, authorizations, regulations, rulings, certificates, orders, directives, contracts, agreements, and other actions made, issued, taken, or entered into under the provisions of Executive Order 11958, as amended, and not revoked, superseded, or otherwise made inapplicable, shall continue in full force and effect until amended, modified, or terminated by appropriate authority'. Own-residual check, reading EO 11958 in full: it delegated functions (sec. 1), set coordination (sec. 2), allocated funds (sec. 3) and, in sec. 4, revoked EO 11501 while saving actions taken under that order; the actions taken under EO 11958 (the departments' export and import control regulations, delegations and licensing decisions) are exactly what EO 13637 sec. 4 keeps in force. So the functions and funds are transferred forward by EO 13637 secs. 1 and 3, and actions taken under the order accrue under sec. 4: transferred_or_accrued, not none. The S4 prefill ('review'), the FULL_AND_PARTIAL conflict and the current-law lead are resolved on that ground. All other clauses depended on the Committee's existence, which ended under the order's own terms at a date not recorded in held sources, or, if extended, no later than EO 12110's revocation effective December 31, 1978. EO 12110 itself describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed. Those first ends and the whole-order end are left open rather than inferred from the June 11, 1977 deadline. EO 11992 (May 24, 1977; 42 FR 27195-27196, held official FR scan text) established the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. All fourteen operative clauses (Secs. 1-8, subsections separated) are quoted verbatim from the held OCR text. The order set its own end in Sec. 8 (termination on December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended); that end did not occur because EO 12110 (sec. 1-101(i), effective December 31, 1978) continued the Committee until December 31, 1980, and EO 12258 (sec. 1-101(g), effective December 31, 1980) continued it until December 31, 1982, so the chain is unbroken. Before that extended term ran out, EO 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, item (b)) revoked EO 11992 and terminated the Committee; EO 12305 states no other effective date, so every clause's first end is May 5, 1981, which is also the whole-order end. No amendment of EO 11992 was found (OFR 1989 disposition table: 'Continued by EOs 12110, 12258; Revoked by EO 12305'; USC note at 28 U.S.C. pt. I agrees). The revocation leaves no savings or residual effect.

EO 12305 revokes the whole order and terminates the committee without any savings, transfer or wind-up provision. The order itself creates no property, office tenure or entitlement that could survive: members served without compensation (travel expenses only, payable while engaged in the work), its post-service ineligibility rule is a provision of the revoked order and fell with it, and no function was transferred to another body. No continuing residual found in the order, in EO 12305, or in the later-source searches recorded below.

EO 12075 (Interagency Coordinating Council), signed 1978-08-16. The order establishes the Interagency Coordinating Council (Section 1-101), lists its member agencies (1-102), provides for a Chairperson (1-103), sets functions (1-201 to 1-205), administrative provisions (1-301 to 1-303) and a report by the Chairperson to the President (1-304). Its held text has no sunset or termination provision. EO 12148 Section 5-210 later added an agency to the membership list in Section 1-102. First end: Section 14 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12075," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18, 43 FR 37161-37162), read in full from the held FR text, places 17 positions in level IV and 14 positions in level V of the Executive Schedule (secs. 1-101, 1-102), preserves the appointments of incumbents (sec. 1-201) and revokes EO 11861, as amended (sec. 1-202). The order has no sunset, termination or report clause. The machine own-term kinds ('condition' and an undated 'fixed_term', plus a quoted conflict) are all noise: they were picked up from other documents printed on the same Federal Register pages (the public-inspection notice, a list of rules going into effect, and a Governors' proclamation), not from the order. EO 12154 (signed 1979-09-04, 44 FR 51965, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_12154) sec. 1-202 revokes it 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing. Three orders amended EO 12076 before that and were read in full: EO 12099 (1978-11-17) moves the Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, from level V (item 1-102(e)) to level IV (new item (r)); EO 12111 (1979-01-02) deletes the Interior position in item 1-102(g) and adds a Commerce position as (s); EO 12119 (1979-02-14) deletes the Justice position in item 1-101(f) and inserts a Treasury position. Those three items therefore have an earlier first end than the revocation (1-102(e) on 1978-11-17, 1-102(g) on 1979-01-02, 1-101(f) on 1979-02-14), and the two list leads carry all three amendments as later events; every other clause ends with the revocation. Inventory correction: the dossier's 31 item clauses mis-bound items (q) and (n-dup2) and omit secs. 1-201 and 1-202 (see inventory_overrides, 35 clauses). A by-number scan finds EO 12076 named only in EO 12099, 12111, 12119 and 12154; the dossier conflict (a quarantined Stage 19 relationship) is addressed in conflict_resolutions. EO 12154's own sec. 1-201 and the successor placements are described in savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_12154 (EO 12154, 44 FR 51965, read once in full): sec. 1-101 and 1-102 place positions in levels IV and V, sec. 1-201 provides that 'Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to terminate or otherwise affect the appointment, or to require the reappointment, of any occupant of any position listed in Section 1-1 of this Order who was the occupant of that position immediately prior to the issuance of this Order', and sec. 1-202 revokes EO 12076, as amended. The sec. 1-201 proviso protects the incumbents of the positions that EO 12154 itself lists, which re-places a number of the positions that EO 12076 placed (for example the Senior Adviser to the Secretary of State, the Administrator of ADAMHA, the Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs, the Special Assistant to the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations and the Executive Director of the PBGC). Own-residual check, reading EO 12076 in full: it placed positions in the Executive Schedule and, in sec. 1-201, protected incumbents' appointments; the placements are functions of the order that EO 12154 carries forward by re-listing the positions, and appointments made while EO 12076 was in force are not undone by its revocation. Positions that EO 12154 does not re-list lose their Executive Schedule placement; the order created no other right, fund or property. The S4 prefill ('review') is resolved as transferred_or_accrued (functions carried forward and appointments preserved), on the same ground as the Executive Schedule successor chain. Bounded search: EO 12076, 12099, 12111, 12119 and 12154 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts.

EO 12077 (signed 1978-08-18) is a one-person exemption under section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code: Roy T. Sessums, Member of the Mississippi River Commission, is exempted from mandatory retirement for age until October 1, 1978. The held Federal Register text of the order was read in full and is a single operative clause (the recital, the finding of public interest, and the exempting sentence). The order ends by its own terms on 1978-10-01 (inclusive; exclusive alternative 1978-09-30, owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until dates). Searches judged adequate: U.S. Code and eCFR (no hit naming the order), the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note catalog, and a Cruden regex search of the held order texts for the person's surname, run by the producer, which found the chain members recorded above and nothing else. Whether the person left office on or before the stated date is not in any held source and is not asserted.

EO 12305 of May 5, 1981, item (c), revoked 'Executive Order No. 12084 ... as amended by Executive Order 12097' and terminated the Commission, effective on signing, so every clause first ends on May 5, 1981, the whole-order end. The identity quarantine is resolved: the held page 43 FR 44815 is headed 'Executive Order 12084 - September 27,1978'. USC note at 28 U.S.C. 133 and the OFR 1989 table agree. No savings provision exists.

EO 12305 revokes the whole order and terminates the committee without any savings, transfer or wind-up provision. EO 12145 (signed 1979-07-18, 44 FR 42653-42656), read in full from the held official FR text: secs. 1-101 to 1-112 deem amendments to the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to conform the Foreign Service retirement system to six Civil Service Retirement laws listed in Annex I, with Annexes II-IV setting out the deemed text; sec. 1-113 revokes EO 11952. It has no term or sunset. EO 12292 sec. 10(l) revokes it, effective as of February 15, 1981 under EO 12292 sec. 11 (signed February 23, 1981). Inventory: the dossier's 3 clauses start at sec. 1-101(b) and stop at sec. 1-113, omitting sec. 1-101(a) and all four Annexes, which the order makes part of itself; one override gives 18 clauses (secs. 1-101(a) to 1-113 and Annexes I-IV) from the same held text. D6 / earlier-end test: the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 12145 named as an order only in EO 12292 sec. 10(l) (other hits are pay-table figures in EO 11524 and the FR page number 9 FR 12145 in EO 9488); OFR catalog notes record only the EO 12292 revocation (and this order's own revocation of EO 11952); the U.S. Code and eCFR searches have no hit. The dossier's second ACT record 'EO:12145>EO:9452' and its 1944 chain date are an artifact: its source is the February 25, 1981 FR issue containing EO 12292, whose sec. 10(a) names EO 9452; the acting instrument is EO 12292, not EO 9452. No order amended, suspended or ended any clause before 1981-02-15, so no later event is attached. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

Reading record LSP-EO_12292 (EO 12292, 46 FR 13967-13968, official FR text read once in full): issued 'to conform existing Executive Orders to changes resulting from' the Foreign Service Act of 1980; secs. 1-9 amend EO 9154, 10471, 10624, 10903, 11034, 11219, 12137, 12163 and 12228; sec. 10 'The following are hereby revoked:' thirteen items, among them '(l) Executive Order No. 12145 of July 18,1979'; sec. 11 'This Order shall be effective as of February 15,1981.' (signed February 23, 1981, so the revocation runs from February 15, 1981). There is no savings, continuation, transfer or exception wording for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 12145 in full (secs. 1-101 to 1-113 and Annexes I-IV): under sec. 805 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 it extended six Civil Service Retirement laws to the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System by deeming amendments to FSA secs. 804, 811, 821, 851 and 864 (survivor-annuity marriage period, minimum annuity, a flat annuity increase, recomputation for unmarried annuitants and on a beneficiary's death, annual notice, World War II internment credit, allotments and court-ordered payments), and revoked EO 11952. Annuities increased or recomputed, internment service credited, elections and notices received, and court-ordered payments made before 1981-02-15 are completed acts and rights that matured under the order; EO 12292 does not undo them. The 1946 Act provisions the order deemed amended were themselves replaced by the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (effective February 15, 1981, the date EO 12292 adopts); any benefit paid after that date rests on the 1980 Act, not on this order (the 1980 Act's text is not held and is not relied on). No clause of EO 12145 continues; state transferred_or_accrued records the accrued benefits and completed acts.
