EO 12150 (signed July 23, 1979; 44 FR 43455), read in full in the held FR text, has one operative sentence: Section 1(b) of EO 11896 (Jan. 13, 1976, establishing the U.S. Sinai Support Mission; I read its sec. 1 in the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11896.txt) 'is hereby amended to read' a new paragraph (b) that redefines the Mission's duties by reference to the 1975 Basic Agreement 'as superseded by the Treaty of Peace' of March 26, 1979 and Article VII of the Appendix to Annex I. EO 12227 (signed July 22, 1980; 45 FR 49237), read in full from the held actor text, states that 'Sections 1(b) and 1(c) of Executive Order No. 11896 ..., as amended, are hereby further amended to read as follows' and prints an entirely new paragraph (b) (the Mission 'assist[s] in the implementation of the provisions of Annex I and the Appendix to Annex I' of the Treaty by verification tasks). The text inserted by EO 12150 therefore ceased to exist in EO 11896 when EO 12227 took effect; the OFR catalog confirms both as amendments of EO 11896. EO 12227 states no effective date and has no savings or transition clause, so it took effect on signing, 1980-07-22. Later events (EO 12357 of Apr. 6, 1982 adding wind-down sec. 2(g); EO 12553 of Feb. 25, 1986 revoking EO 11896 and its amendments) post-date the first end and are not used. Searches: OFR catalog 'Amended by' list for EO 11896 (EO 12150, 12227, 12357) shows no amendment of (b) between 1979-07-23 and 1980-07-22; U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches have 0 hits.

That fixed end date is the order's own term, not a reporting deadline: when it arrived the extension the order granted was used up. EO 12351 of March 9, 1982 gave a new, separate extension to March 10, 1983 (recorded as a later event; it does not amend EO 12295), and the series continued by annual orders. The 1987 revocation by EO 12608 Sec. 1 therefore follows an earlier actual cessation and is recorded as a later formal event. First end of the clause and whole-order end: March 10, 1982, by expiry under the order's own terms. The USC note at 42 U.S.C. 2155 ('extended the period ... to Mar. 10, 1982') and the OFR 1989 table ('Revoked by EO 12608') are consistent with this.

The order's only effect was to keep the statutory cooperation period open until March 10, 1982. Cooperation after that date rests on EO 12351 and later annual extensions (successor authority). EO 12400 (Jan. 3, 1983; 48 FR 381) established the President's Commission on Strategic Forces under FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern that Commission. Original sec. 4(b) ended it 30 days after its report (due February 18, 1983). EO 12406 (Feb. 18, 1983) moved the report deadline to April 15, 1983 and the end to 60 days after reporting; EO 12424 (June 10, 1983), which records the report as 'dated April 11, 1983', gave the Commission a new review mandate (sec. 2(a)), a report deadline of December 15, 1983 (sec. 2(b)) and a fixed end: 'terminate on January 3, 1984, unless sooner extended' (sec. 4(b)). EO 12424 was signed on the 60th day after April 11, 1983, so the Commission did not lapse before the extension (if the report reached the President later than its date, the margin is larger). No later extension appears in the held order texts, the OFR catalog notes or the 1989 Codification (amendments listed: EOs 12406, 12424), and the Commission is not in continuance order EO 12489. The Commission and every clause therefore ended on January 3, 1984 (whole-order end). EO 12534 sec. 3(k), effective September 30, 1985, is a later cleanup revocation. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. No human certification is asserted.

Neither EO 12400 nor the revoking EO 12534 contains a savings clause, and EO 12534 sec. 3 states that the committees it lists had already terminated. Members served without compensation; the sec. 3(a) direction that information supplied to or developed by the Commission not be available for public inspection applies only 'to the extent permitted by law', so it added no authority of its own that could outlast the order; and the Defense support and FACA delegation in secs. 3(c) and 4(a) applied only to the Commission. No rights, entitlements, property, delegations or functions outside the body itself were created, so nothing survives its termination; reimbursements and support given while it existed are completed transactions, not continuing effects. The order establishes the President's Child Safety Partnership of not more than 26 members (Section 1), its functions, with a final report due by April 29, 1987 (Section 2), administration (Section 3) and general provisions (Section 4). First end: Section 4(c) of the order provides that the Partnership shall terminate on April 29, 1987, or 60 days after submitting its final report, whichever is earlier. The fixed date is the latest date on which the Partnership could end, so I record 1987-04-29 as the first end by the order's own terms (read inclusively: the Partnership exists through April 29, 1987). The report-relative alternative could have ended it earlier; the held packet has no dated record of the final report, so that possibility is disclosed and no earlier date is claimed. Section 3(d) of EO 12610 later revoked the order, effective September 30, 1987, which is after the sunset and is a later event. The order transfers Defense Production Act responsibilities of the General Services Administration to the Department of Defense by amending section 303 of EO 10480 (Administrator of General Services replaced by Secretary of Defense) and section 604 of EO 10480 (General Services Administration replaced by Department of Defense, and Administrator of General Services replaced by Secretary of Defense). The order states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the amendment is therefore not exhausted on signing. EO 10480 was superseded or revoked by EO 12919 (signed 1994-06-03; 59 FR 29525, Federal Register of June 7, 1994) in section 904(a)(3), and EO 12919 section 904(a)(11) supersedes or revokes EO 12773 except that part that amends section 604 of EO 10480. Both parts therefore end on the same date: the section 303 part by the express supersession of EO 12773, and the section 604 part because its parent, EO 10480, was revoked in the same order on the same day. EO 12919 has no delayed-effective-date wording for section 904, so the date is its signing date, 1994-06-03. The dossier has one clause (the whole order) which covers the single ordering sentence. EO 12817 (signed 1992-10-21, 57 FR 48433-48434), read in full from the held official FR text: preamble (IEEPA, NEA, UNPA sec. 5; UNSCR 778; the EO 12722 emergency); sec. 1 Treasury authority; sec. 2 compelled transfer of Iraqi petroleum proceeds to the FRBNY; sec. 3 FRBNY as fiscal agent; sec. 4 acquittance and immunity; sec. 5 definition of 'United States financial institution'; sec. 6 Treasury rules and redelegation; sec. 7 no private rights; sec. 8 effective immediately and transmittal. It has no term or sunset. EO 13350 (preamble) revokes it in full as an order based on the EO 12722 emergency, effective 12:01 a.m. EDT 2004-07-30 (sec. 10). Inventory: the dossier's 9 clauses cover the order without a textual gap, but its 'sec1' span runs through sec. 2 and it separates the bare heading 'Sec. 8.' from (a); one override splits secs. 1 and 2 and joins the heading to (a), giving 9 clauses. D6 / earlier-end test: the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 12817 only in EO 13350 (plus the FR page number 33 FR 12817 in EO 11429); OFR catalog notes record only the EO 13350 revocation (and 'see' notes from EO 12722 and 12724, cross-references); the U.S. Code and eCFR searches have no hit. No order amended, suspended or ended any clause before 2004-07-30, so no later event is attached. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

Reading record LSP-EO_13350 (EO 13350, 69 FR 46055-46057, read once in full; reused from Lambertini scale after re-verifying text_sha256 904607b3... on disk; Annex pages 4-13 are images): the preamble terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12722 and revokes EO 12722, 12724, 12734, 12743, 12751 and 12817 'that are based on that national emergency'; sec. 1 provides, under NEA sec. 202(a) (50 U.S.C. 1622(a)), that the termination 'shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date', and continues under IEEPA sec. 207(a) the blocking of property blocked under EO 12722 or 12724 only; secs. 2-8 set up new measures under the 2003 emergency (EO 13303/13315); sec. 9 disclaims private rights; sec. 10 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. EDT July 30, 2004. There is no transfer of functions and no exception for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 12817 in full (preamble, secs. 1-8): it delegated IEEPA 203/205 and UNPA authority to the Treasury Secretary to carry out UNSCR 778 (sec. 1), compelled U.S. financial institutions to transfer to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York funds representing proceeds of Iraqi petroleum sales (sec. 2), authorized the FRBNY to hold, invest or transfer them for the UN escrow (sec. 3), and made compliance a full acquittance with good-faith immunity (sec. 4). Transfers made, funds held or passed to the United Nations escrow, and the acquittances and immunities that attached before 2004-07-30 are actions taken and rights matured under the order; EO 13350 sec. 1 (NEA 202(a)) expressly leaves them unaffected, and sec. 4 itself says the order has no effect on rights existing before transfer. The IEEPA 207(a) continuation in EO 13350 sec. 1 covers property blocked under EO 12722/12724, not any clause of EO 12817. No clause of EO 12817 continues; state transferred_or_accrued records the preserved completed effects. S1 transfer-wording prefill (review) resolved to transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: the order and the ending instrument read in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

EO 12852 (signed June 29, 1993; 58 FR 35841-35842), read in full from the held FR text, created the President's Council on Sustainable Development for 2 years (sec. 4(b)). Four later orders amended it: EO 12855 (1993-07-19, administrative support moved to Interior), EO 12965 (1995-06-27, term to June 29, 1997), EO 12980 (1995-11-17, 29 members), EO 13053 (1997-06-30, 35 members, Interior to Energy, term to February 28, 1999) and EO 13114 (1999-02-25, term to June 30, 1999), each read in full from the held FR text. Their combined effect is that the Council's term ran out by its own terms on June 30, 1999. EO 13138 (signed September 30, 1999, effective that day under sec. 9) lists the Council among committees that 'have terminated and whose work is completed' and revokes the order; it is recorded as a later cleanup event. The first end of every Council clause is therefore 1999-06-30; sec. 4(c)'s revocation of EO 12737 was a one-time act complete on 1993-06-29. The dossier's eleven scopes cover every operative paragraph and were kept. The ofr_catalog search found 8 hits and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches 7 each, consistent with the amendments and the revocation; no order extended the Council beyond June 30, 1999. Savings: see savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13138 (EO 13138, 64 FR 53879-53881, read once in full): sec. 1 continues sixteen advisory committees to 2001-09-30 (EO 12852 is not among them); sec. 2 reassigns the President's Federal Advisory Committee Act functions for those sixteen committees to the listed agency heads; sec. 3(a)-(g) revokes seven committee orders 'which established committees that have terminated and whose work is completed', EO 12852 in sec. 3(f); secs. 4-8 supersede and amend other orders; sec. 9 makes it effective 1999-09-30. There is no savings, pending-matter or exception clause, and the sec. 2 transfer reaches only the sec. 1 committees. EO 12963 (June 14, 1995, 60 FR 31905) directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish the Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS (up to 30 members; 35 after EO 13009), defines its advisory functions, administration and general provisions. The complete held original was read; the dossier inventory (lead, 1(a), 1(b), 2, 3(a), 3(b), 3(c), 4(a), 4(b)) is complete. The order itself states no end (dossier own_terms hold only generic 'condition' wording on funding and appropriations, not an end). Amendments: EO 13009 (June 14, 1996) replaces '30' with '35' in the second sentence of section 1(a); read in full, effective on signing; attached to section 1(a). No other order amends it. Continuation: the Council is a Federal Advisory Committee Act body, so it stands only while continued. The held continuation orders EO 13708 (2015), 13811 (2017), 13889 (2019), 14048 (2021), 14109 (2023) and EO 14354 (Sept. 29, 2025) each list 'Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS; Executive Order 12963, as amended'; the latest, EO 14354 section 1(f), continues it until September 30, 2027, effective September 30, 2025 (sec. 4), and sec. 3 supersedes the 2023 continuation. EO 14354 is the held, attributed current basis for every clause: it is a later order that continues the Council through the cutoff of 2026-10-14. The dossier's 'target provision not located' lines for EOs 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109 and 14354 were each resolved by reading the held actor text: all six are 'Continuance (or Reestablishment) of Certain Federal Advisory Committees' orders listing the Council; none ends or narrows it. EO 13703 (2015, HIV strategy) sec. 5 also relies on the Council. Sunset note for the reviewer: the only sunset is the 2027-09-30 continuation date in the later order, not in EO 12963 itself; it falls after the cutoff, so the Council stands continued at 2026-10-14. If the reviewer reads the brief's 'body with its own sunset' rule to cover a renewable continuation date, this claim is PARTIAL_SCOPE. D6: searched (1) the dossier chain (EO 13009), (2) EDGES.csv (EO 13009 amends; EOs 13708, 13811, 14354 continue), (3) all 6,652 held fr-originals texts to EO 14435 for number citations in word and bare form and for 'Advisory Council on HIV' wording in orders from EO 14100 onward (only EOs 14109 and 14354, both continuations), (4) the machine searches (U.S. Code to 2026-10-09, eCFR to 2026-10-14, OFR catalog 4 hits). No termination order was found. The EO 13306 original-as-basis pattern is NOT used here. No human certification is asserted.

No savings, transfer or accrued-rights clause appears in EO 12963 or EO 13009. The Council is advisory only, creates no rights (sec. 4(b)) and its continuation by successive orders is the only temporal feature; nothing is left in a former body.

EO 13101 (signed 1998-09-14, 63 FR 49643-49651), read in full from the held FR text, directs executive agencies to prefer recycled and environmentally preferable products and to prevent waste and recycle: it defines terms (Part 2), creates a Steering Committee, a Federal Environmental Executive, a Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives (Part 3), sets acquisition-planning, affirmative-procurement, EPA-designation, paper-content and agency-goal duties with many dated and reporting provisions (Parts 4-6), and adds applicability, recycling-program, training and awards provisions (Parts 7-8) and the revocation of EO 12873 (sec. 901). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause; every timed provision is a performance, action or reporting deadline, not an end. EO 13423 (signed 2007-01-24) sec. 11(a)(i) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out as earlier ends or changes: the dossier's 'target provision not located' leads (EO 12843, 12845, 12856, 12902, 12969, 13031, 13134, 13148, 13149) are OFR 'See' cross-references in both directions and operative-text mentions; none amends, extends or revokes EO 13101 (EO 13134 sec. 7(b) borrows its definition of 'biobased product'; EO 13148 secs. 306, 307, 403(b), 503(b), 1001 and 1008 and EO 13149 refer to its sections). The by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13101 named only in EO 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423 (the other hits are page, document or U.S. Code numbers, for example 42 U.S.C. 13101-13109). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording, which does not revive EO 13101. The dossier's inventory was corrected: the issuing paragraph was added, mislabelled scopes (sec302-g-2 to -5, sec302-b-dup2, sec402-b/c/d-dup2) were renamed to the sections the text shows, the seven list items of sec. 302(a)(1) were merged into it, sec. 402(d)/403(a) and sec. 901/902 were split where a span held two sections, and page furniture and part headings were cut from the span ends. Limitations: bodies formed under the order (the Steering Committee, Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives) may have had their own charter lives, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (a claim-kit rebuild changed only the chain's generic_refs_excluded count 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts are not held.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13101 in full (secs. 101-903): sec. 901 revoked EO 12873 of October 20, 1993 on signing, 1998-09-14, a completed act on another order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13101 without any revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive the order it revoked, so EO 12873 stays revoked: an effect of EO 13101 survives it (accrued). EO 13423 also restates much of EO 13101's machinery as new duties of its own (Steering Committee sec. 4(a), Federal Environmental Executive sec. 6, biobased and recycled-content acquisition and 30 percent post-consumer paper sec. 2(d), waste prevention and recycling programs sec. 2(e)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902). The three current-law leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) cite EO 13101; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: the state is transferred_or_accrued because of the completed revocation of EO 12873 and the successor duties; the prefill gave no state. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

express revocation by EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(i) ('Executive Order 13101 of September 14, 1998' in the list that begins 'The following are revoked'); EO 13423 states no effective date and no delayed-effect wording for sec. 11(a), so the revocation took effect on signing, January 24, 2007 (printed 72 FR 3919-3923, January 26, 2007)

EO 13109 (signed 1998-12-17; 63 FR 70631, Federal Register of 1998-12-22, FR Doc. 98-34034) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13109.txt. It closes executive departments and agencies and excuses employees from duty on one named day (Christmas Eve, December 24, 1998), lets agency heads keep offices open for stated reasons, and treats that day as within the scope of EO 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave. Every command is tied to that single day, so each clause ends by its own terms on 1998-12-24 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading would end the commands when that day began). A by-number search of the held order texts finds no later order citing this order, and the three machine searches record no later amendment, revocation or supersession. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is held. Own terms: the order states one calendar day and no other end. Held later instruments: a by-number search of all held order texts (Cruden, 33,118 held texts) finds only this order's own text; the three machine searches return no amendment, revocation or supersession.","independent_command_check":"No independent continuing command: the authority recital, the agency-head determination and the pay-and-leave treatment all concern the named day only. Section 4 states that the order applies to the Federal Government only and does not direct State or local departments or agencies; it limits the reach of sections 1 through 3 and imposes no separate duty.","savings_check":"Accrued pay and leave for the named day stand on EO 11582 and the cited statutes; nothing in the order continues after the day.","scope_check":"The order is a one-day measure; its inventory is its numbered sections. No partial amendment, extension or revocation of any section is held."}

Employees excused from duty on the named day were excused under the order, and pay and leave for that day are governed by EO 11582 and the cited statutes, which the order only applied to the day; those accrued pay and leave effects rest on the cited authorities and do not keep the order operative after 1998-12-24. No held source shows any pending matter, exception or savings clause in the order.

EO 13128 (signed June 25, 1999; 64 FR 34703, June 28, 1999) implements the Chemical Weapons Convention and the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Act. It designates the Department of State as the United States National Authority (section 1), sets up an interagency coordinating group (section 2), directs State and Commerce to issue implementing regulations (section 3), authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to obtain warrants, suspend or revoke export privileges and run section 501(a) proceedings (section 4), authorizes agency functions and assistance to facilities (sections 5 and 6), lets the National Authority decide on disclosure of confidential business information (section 7), adds a subsection (e) to section 3 of EO 12938 (section 8), routes possible 18 U.S.C. 229 violations to the FBI (section 9), and closes with a no-rights clause and an effective-date and transmittal clause (sections 10 and 11). I read the complete held official Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of fifteen clauses covers every section and subsection; I confirmed it without correction. No section has a fixed end date, sunset or ending condition. The machine chain lists EO 13206 (April 4, 2001) and EO 13382 (June 28, 2005) as amending events, but I read both complete held texts and neither names EO 13128: EO 13206 deals with the Export Administration Act and EO 12924, and EO 13382 amends section 4(a) of EO 12938, not section 3. The dossier's number search of the held order texts finds no order other than EO 13128 itself that cites it. The current-law and catalog machine searches (selected below after reading their coverage notes) record no order that revokes, supersedes or amends EO 13128. Section 8 is a self-executing amendment of another order; I record it as performed on the effective date and separate the inserted subsection, which is text of EO 12938, from this order's own commands. The other fourteen clauses are standing organizational, delegation and authorization provisions of the order, still in force on 2026-10-14 on the original text read with the bounded searches; the legal sources the machine searches point to (the U.S. Code note and 15 CFR and 22 CFR provisions that cite the order) are pointers whose text is not held, so they are not relied on as quoted authority.

EO 13137 (signed 1999-09-15; 64 FR 50733, Federal Register of 1999-09-20, FR Doc. 99-24582) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13137.txt. It further amends EO 12975 (National Bioethics Advisory Commission): section 1 restates section 3 of the parent, section 2 adds a new section 4 (membership of not more than 18, member terms and a Chairperson), and section 3 corrects a cross-reference, renumbers sections 4 through 7 as 5 through 8 and, in section 3(c), changes the termination date in new section 8(b) from October 3, 1999 to October 3, 2001. First end for every clause: the Commission's own fixed sunset. The termination section as written by EO 13046 (62 FR 27685, held Federal Register text) reads in part "shall terminate on October 3, 1999, unless extended by the President prior" to that date; this order's section 3(c) moved the date to October 3, 2001. The Commission therefore terminated on October 3, 2001, recorded inclusive (the exclusive reading, that it ends when that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see), unless an extension issued first. A by-number search of the held order texts for the parent, EO 12975, finds EO 13018, EO 13046, EO 13137 and EO 13316 (Federal Register copies, and American Presidency Project copies of 13018, 13046, 13137 and 13316) and EO 14096, which cites the parent only as a standard of ethics for the protection of human subjects; none extends the Commission past October 3, 2001. Every clause rewrites or adds text of the parent, which operated only through the Commission, so each ends with the Commission; the 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling leaves a clause with its own fixed date unaffected, and the sunset here is a fixed date. Later event after the end: EO 13316 (signed 2003-09-17; 68 FR 55255, Federal Register of 2003-09-23) section 3(b) lists Executive Order 12975, as amended by Executive Orders 13018, 13046 and 13137, among the orders revoked as establishing committees that have terminated or whose work is completed, and section 6 makes it effective September 30, 2003. A by-number search of the held order texts for EO 13137 finds only this order's own Federal Register text; EO 13316 names it in a list that the number pattern does not match and was read directly. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

EO 13147 (2000-03-07), 65 FR 13233 machine text of the Federal Register pages (original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original, no page check required). Secs. 1-3(d) establish the White House Commission on Complementary and Alternative Medicine Policy, give it functions (a report to the President), and provide its members' pay, funding and FACA handling; every one is an incident of the Commission. Sec. 3(e): "The Commission shall terminate 2 years from the date of this order unless extended by the President prior to such date." 2000-03-07 plus 2 years = 2002-03-07 (anniversary convention). The condition 'unless extended' was searched: EO 13167 (2000-09-15) changes only sec. 1 membership; EO 13316 (2003-09-17, effective 2003-09-30) revokes the order, with the Commission described as a committee that 'terminated or whose work is completed'; the U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 287c-21 records the same revocation and no extension (editorial lead only). No extension order is held. The 2003 revocation is later than the term date and is not the first end.

EO 13148 (signed 2000-04-21, 65 FR 24595-24606), read in full from the held FR text, makes agency heads responsible for environmental management and sets goals (Part 2: environmental management systems, compliance audits, right-to-know reporting, 40 percent toxic-release and 50 percent use-reduction goals by December 31, 2006, phase-out planning for Class I ozone-depleting substances by 2010), planning and accountability duties (Part 3), management-system, audit, awards, training, compliance-assistance and assurance duties with 4- to 24-month clocks (Part 4), emergency-planning and toxic-chemical reporting and reduction provisions (Part 5), landscaping (Part 6), acquisition and procurement limits (Part 7), national-security exemptions and OMB compliance modification (Part 8), general provisions including the revocation of EO 12843, 12856, 12969, a 1994 memorandum and section 1-4 of EO 12088 (Part 9) and definitions (Part 10). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause. The dossier's undated 'fixed_term' own-terms (the 'within 12 months after environmentally benign pressure sensitive adhesives ... become commercially available' clock in sec. 702 and the exemption provisions in sec. 801) are conditional action clocks and exemption wording, not ends; December 31, 2006 target dates in secs. 204, 205 and 503(a) passed 24 days before the revocation and are lapsed performance deadlines, not ends. EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(iv) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out: the dossier's lead ACT:EO:13148>EO:13693 is spurious: EO 13693 sec. 16(d) amends EO 13327 sec. 3(b)(vi), striking the citation of EO 13148 there, and amends nothing in EO 13148 (the dossier flags the large EO 13693 context for reading before scope is decided; read, it holds no such provision); the 'target provision not located' leads (EO 13101, 13123, 13134) are EO 13148's own citations of those orders; the by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13148 named only in EO 13327 (a citation), 13423 and 13693 (the other hits are page numbers or a hash). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording. Inventory corrections: the issuing paragraph was added; heading-only fragments (secs. 305, 403, 404, 405, 406, 601, 701, 704, 902) were merged into their first subsection; the sentences the dossier cut mid-way in secs. 501(b)/(d), 501(e) and 503(b) were rejoined and the duplicate-suffixed scope of sec. 501(d) was renamed; page furniture and part headings were cut from span ends. Limitations: the Interagency Environmental Leadership Workgroup (sec. 306) and other bodies formed under the order may have had charter lives of their own, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (only chain.generic_refs_excluded 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts and Code note are not held.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13148 in full (secs. 101-1009): sec. 901 revoked EO 12843, EO 12856, the Executive Memorandum on Environmentally Beneficial Landscaping of April 26, 1994, EO 12969 and section 1-4 'Pollution Control Plan' of EO 12088 on signing, 2000-04-21: completed acts on other instruments, one of them a partial revocation of a surviving order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13148 without revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked, so those stay revoked: an effect of EO 13148 survives it (accrued); the U.S. Code note to 42 U.S.C. 4321 still prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 sec. 901. EO 13423 restates the environmental-management subject as new duties of its own (toxic and hazardous chemical and waste reduction sec. 2(e), environmental management systems sec. 3(b), compliance audits sec. 3(c), reporting sec. 3(g)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse; the statutory reporting duties the order repeats (EPCRA sec. 313, PPA sec. 6607, sec. 902(c)) rest on those statutes independently. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902(a)). The three current-law leads (42 U.S.C. 4321 note, 33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E) cite EO 13148; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (2000-12-28, Revocation of Executive Order 12834). Inventory: the authority recital ending 'it is hereby ordered as follows:' (characters 676 to 947, the dossier's clause) is not operative. The order's two operative sentences follow it: the revocation of EO 12834 of January 20, 1993 (Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees), effective at noon January 20, 2001 (characters 948 to 1101), and the sentence that employees and former employees subject to the commitments in EO 12834 will not be subject to those commitments after the effective date of the order (characters 1103 to 1267). The inventory override replaces the recital with these two clauses. The revocation is self-executing: it was performed by operation of the order at its stated effective moment, so that clause is exhausted by performance on 2001-01-20. The release sentence states the consequence of that revocation; once the revocation took effect nothing remained for EO 13184 to do, so it is exhausted on the same date, and the resulting freedom from the commitments is an accrued effect of the completed revocation and not a continuing command of EO 13184. A by-number search of the held order texts for EO 13184 finds only this order's own text, and the three machine searches record no amendment, revocation or supersession of this order (current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 0). its final report." That clause is triggered by the date of a report and is not an end under owner ruling 2026-10-21-report-deadline; the report date is not held in any source in the repository, so it is disclosed here and not recorded as an end. EO 13274 (signed September 18, 2002; 67 FR 59449, September 23, 2002) states a policy of environmental stewardship and expedited review of high-priority transportation infrastructure projects (section 1), directs agencies and the Secretary of Transportation to act (section 2), establishes the Transportation Infrastructure Streamlining Task Force and sets its functions and membership (section 3), requires an annual Task Force report (section 4), preserves OMB functions (section 5) and states a no-rights clause (section 6). I read the complete held official Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of thirteen clauses covers every section and subsection; the fragment labelled section 2 covers the heading and subsection (a), the fragment labelled section 3 covers the heading and the opening of subsection (a), and the fragment labelled section 3(i) completes subsection (a). I confirmed the inventory without correction. The only held later order that names EO 13274 is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, 68 FR 10619), whose section 2 inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security into the Task Force membership list in section 3(b); I read the complete held section and the effective-date section 92 of that order (effective March 1, 2003). Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 that is a later amendment, not an end. The order has no sunset. The annual report in section 4 is a recurring duty and its timing is not an end. No held source revokes or supersedes EO 13274 or shows the Task Force abolished. The standing clauses are operative on 2026-10-14 on the original text read with the bounded searches. A held source-ladder text of 46 CFR 393.3 (2025 edition) refers to projects on the Secretary's list of high-priority transportation infrastructure projects under EO 13274; it was returned for a different request and is not a registered source of this claim, so I treat it only as a pointer and rely on the original text and the searches.

EO 13561 of December 22, 2010 (Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay; 75 FR 81817, Federal Register of December 29, 2010) sets pay rates for the statutory pay systems, the Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative and judicial salaries, uniformed services, locality-based comparability payments and administrative law judges by attached schedules, and in its section 8 supersedes its predecessor. Its section 7 makes Schedule 8 effective January 1, 2011 and the other schedules effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2011. Section 8 reads "Executive Order 13525 of December 23, 2009, is superseded." It is a self-executing supersession with no deferred effective date, performed when EO 13561 took effect on signing (2010-12-22); the project records the same kind of clause that way elsewhere. That clause's first end is 2010-12-22. Every other clause ends with the supersession of this order by EO 13594 of December 19, 2011 (76 FR 80191, Federal Register of December 23, 2011), whose section 8 reads "Executive Order 13561 of December 22, 2010, is superseded." That sentence is an express supersession of the whole order and carries no effective-date qualifier of its own; EO 13594 section 7, which gives its own schedules the effective dates January 1, 2012 (Schedule 8) and the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2012 (the other schedules), speaks only of the "other schedules contained herein" and does not defer section 8. The supersession therefore took effect on signing, 2011-12-19, and that is the first end of the schedule clauses. Disclosed alternative reading: the schedules of EO 13561 continued to govern pay until the new schedules took effect (January 1, 2012 for Schedule 8; the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2012 for the others, a date the held sources do not give). The lead-in of EO 13594 recites that Public Law 111-322 freezes certain pay schedules for civilian Federal employees at 2010 levels through 2012, which accounts for continuity of rates between the two orders without any continuing force in EO 13561. EO 13771 (signed 2017-01-30, 82 FR 9339; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 19 clauses) states the policy of prudent regulatory costs (sec. 1), imposes a two-for-one offset and a cap for fiscal year 2017 (sec. 2), requires annual regulatory cost submissions and allowances from fiscal year 2018 on (sec. 3), defines regulation (sec. 4) and has general provisions (sec. 5). First ends: eighteen clauses end with the order on 2021-01-20 by EO 13992 sec. 2 (LSP-EO_13992); sec. 2(b) is the exception: it is a cap 'for fiscal year 2017' and stopped operating by its own terms when fiscal year 2017 ended on 2017-09-30, so its first end is that earlier own-terms date (cited to the clause's own text; the fiscal-year end is general law, not a held source). The sec. 2 heading 'Regulatory Cap for Fiscal Year 2017' was weighed against paragraphs (a), (c) and (d), which carry no period and are read as running to the revocation; this is the main judgement call in the claim. The whole-order end is the latest first end, 2021-01-20. Other-actor leads: ACT:EO:13771>EO:13777 and >EO:13783 are false positives (EO 13777 sec. 2(a)(i) lists EO 13771 among the initiatives agency officers oversee, and EO 13783 sec. 2(g) asks agencies to coordinate with it; neither revokes, amends or suspends any part of EO 13771). Dossier missing lines 'target provision not located: EO:12866, 13782, 13790, 13817, 13891': EO 12866 predates it; EO 13782 does not name it; EO 13790 (sec. on the task force coordinating with reviews under it), EO 13817 (implement consistently with it) and EO 13891 (lists it as a compliance standard) only refer to it. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. EO 13777 (signed 2017-02-24, 82 FR 12285; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 36 clauses) states the policy of alleviating unnecessary regulatory burdens (sec. 1), has each agency designate a Regulatory Reform Officer (sec. 2), establish a Regulatory Reform Task Force that evaluates existing regulations and reports progress (sec. 3), measure accountability (sec. 4), allows OMB waivers (sec. 5) and has general provisions (sec. 6). Own-terms: only conditions ('unless otherwise designated by the agency head', 'consistent with applicable law'); the 60/90-day periods are performance and report deadlines, never ends. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Dossier missing lines 'target provision not located: EO:12866, 13563, 13771, 13891': EO 12866 (1993), EO 13563 (2011) and EO 13771 (2017-01-30, before EO 13777 of 2017-02-24) predate it and cannot amend it; EO 13891 (2019) only lists EO 13777 as a compliance standard (sec. 4(a)(iii)(D), 4(b)); none amends, suspends or reinstates it. EO 13966 (2020) cites its policy only. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note that EO 13777 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The three dossier machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13777 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13777 is named only in EO 13891 (twice), EO 13966 and EO 13992, all of which cite or refer to it without amending it; no held text amends it. Conflict, savings and the own-residual check are in conflict_resolutions and savings_residuals.

Own-residual check, reading EO 13777 in full (secs. 1-6): sec. 2 had each agency head designate a Regulatory Reform Officer and sec. 3 had each agency establish a Regulatory Reform Task Force (with joint task forces for multi-agency entities); the RROs and task forces were therefore created in the agencies by the order's directions and, on EO 13992's own wording, survive the revocation until abolished by agency action. No function is transferred to a successor and no right is created (sec. 6(c)), so the residual is the accrued positions and entities and not a transfer. rationales.exact_text: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13783 by number in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; the only exception in sec. 7(a) is EO 13834 and the sec. 7(a) list otherwise excepts nothing; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order or act; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13783 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 8(c) disclaims rights) and no continuing body. But parts of it are completed, self-executing acts on OTHER instruments: sec. 3(a) revokes EO 13653 and the Presidential Memoranda of June 25, 2013, November 3, 2015 and September 21, 2016; sec. 3(b) rescinds two Executive Office reports; sec. 5(b) disbands the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases and withdraws six of its technical documents. Revoking EO 13783 does not by itself restore any of them. EO 13990 reinstates only EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum (sec. 4(b)), and sec. 5(b) establishes a new Working Group without reviving the old documents; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds EO 13653 named only in EO 13677, 13683, 13693 and 13783, and no held order reinstates it or the memoranda. Those acts therefore continue independently of EO 13783. S4 prefill ('review', dossier conflict) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not none_after_bounded_search). EO 13921 sec. 6(a) (2020-05-07; effective on signing, no effective-date wording) tells agencies reviewing aquaculture projects to 'use the ''One Federal Decision'' process enhancements described in section 5(b) of Executive Order 13807': an incorporation by reference of sec. 5(b), not an amendment, suspension or revocation of EO 13807, so no later event is attached (EO 13921 is also not among the dossier's evidence records, so it could not be attached); EO 14276 (2025-04-17, 90 FR 16993) says EO 13921 'remains in effect', and the use of the process for aquaculture continues under EO 13921 itself after EO 13807's revocation - see savings_residuals. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts finds EO 13807 named only in EO 13817, 13921, 13990 and 14030, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement of EO 13807 itself is recorded. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but do not name EO 13807 or reinstate it, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Inventory: the dossier's 52 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 7(c). rationales.exact_text: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(b) revokes EO 13807 by number with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; sec. 7(b)'s second sentence only tells the OMB Director and CEQ Chair to 'consider whether to recommend that a replacement order be issued' (a direction to consider, not a transfer). Own-residual check, reading EO 13807 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 7(c) disclaims rights) and no body. Three things need a state. (1) Sec. 6 is a completed act on another instrument: it revoked EO 13690 (Federal Flood Risk Management Standard). EO 13990 did not reinstate EO 13690, so that revocation outlived EO 13807 until EO 14030 sec. 5(e) expressly reinstated EO 13690 on 2021-05-20 (attached as a later event on sec6). (2) Sec. 5(b)'s 'One Federal Decision' process is incorporated by reference in EO 13921 sec. 6(a), which EO 14276 (2025) says remains in effect; the process continues to be directed for aquaculture projects independently of EO 13807 (recorded here; not attachable as a later event because it neither amends, suspends nor revokes the clause and EO 13921 is not among the dossier's evidence records). (3) Functions it assigned or re-delegated (sec. 5(d) CEQ-to-FPISC referrals for EO 13766, sec. 5(f) GSA support and delegations, sec. 5(h) Interior strategy) lapse with the order or rest on 42 U.S.C. 4370m-4370m-12 and the agencies' own authority; EO 13990 sec. 8(a) saves only that statutory authority and moves nothing. S1 prefill ('review', transfer wording) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not transferred_or_accrued and not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13807, EO 13766, EO 13817, EO 13921, EO 13990, EO 14030 and EO 14276 in full or in the cited sections; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435). The present status of the Framework Memorandum of March 20, 2018 and of EO 13690 after the 2025 revocation of EO 14030 are outside this order's lifecycle and not searched.

EO 13828 (signed April 10, 2018, 83 FR 15941-15944), read in full from the held official FR text, states the Principles of Economic Mobility as policy (sec. 2), directs eight Secretaries to review regulations and programs, report within 90 days and take steps to implement recommended administrative actions (sec. 3), defines terms (sec. 4) and has general provisions (sec. 5). It has no term or sunset: the only timing words are the 90-day review and report deadlines in sec. 3, which are deadlines and never ends. EO 14018 sec. 1 (reading record LSP-EO_14018, read once in full) revokes the order with no effective-date wording, effective on signing 2021-02-24. The dossier's ACT record is built on the held official FR text of EO 14018 and carries the sec. 1 sentence naming the order; its scope is whole. The dossier lists no missing provision and no conflict. The dossier's 40 clauses run contiguously from the first section to the signature line, so the inventory is kept as is. D6 (any later event that ended or changed a clause): a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts finds EO 13828 named only in EO 14018 (EO 9805 holds 13828 as a CFR page number); the OFR catalog edges (4 rows) and the USC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note record only the EO 14018 revocation; no amendment, extension or reinstatement appears in those sources. Savings: none_after_bounded_search, see savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_14018 (EO 14018, 86 FR 11855-11856, read once in full): sec. 1 revokes five Executive orders and two memoranda with no effective-date wording; sec. 2 treats rules and policies implementing a listed order as separate acts for the agencies to consider rescinding and abolishes entities created under the listed actions as appropriate and consistent with law; sec. 3(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, transfer of functions or funds, pending-matter clause or exception. The two transfer-wording hits the machine counted are words in the title of a revoked Memorandum ('Delegation of Certain Authority Under the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute'), not an operative transfer. Own-residual check, reading EO 13828 in full (secs. 1-5): it states the Principles of Economic Mobility as policy, directs the review, report and implementation steps and defines terms; it created no office, fund or right, transferred no function and revoked or amended no earlier order. Administrative actions an agency took under sec. 3 are that agency's own acts under its statutes, which EO 14018 sec. 2 treats as separate acts to consider rescinding; sec. 5(c) disclaims private rights. S1 transfer-wording prefill (review) resolved to none_after_bounded_search. EO 13834 (signed 2018-05-17, 83 FR 23771-23774), read in full from the held FR text, sets efficient-operations goals for agencies (secs. 1-2), implementation actions with 45- to 150-day periods (sec. 3), duties of the CEQ Chairman including the continuation of the Steering Committee (sec. 4), of the OMB Director (sec. 5), of the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer (sec. 6) and of agency heads (sec. 7), the revocation of EO 13693 (sec. 8) and limitations, exemptions and general provisions (secs. 9-11). The machine own-term kind is condition only (sec. 11(b)). The order has no sunset or termination clause. Two later orders end it in two steps, which is why its clauses have two different first ends. EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037-7043, held FR text, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990) sec. 7(a) says EO 13834 'is hereby revoked except for sections 6, 7, and 11', with no effective-date wording, so sections 1-5 and 8-10 ended on 2021-01-20; the dossier's machine ACT scope 'partial' for this record is correct, and its ACT record 'ACT:EO:13834>EO:13990' (the official FR text, split across the printed pages 7041-7042) is the first end for those clauses. EO 14057 (signed 2021-12-08, 86 FR 70935-70943, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_14057) sec. 604 revokes EO 13834 in full, with no effective-date wording, so sections 6, 7 and 11 ended on 2021-12-08; the dossier's end ACT record for EO 14057 quotes the American Presidency Project transcription, so that end is cited by ACTOR_TEXT:EO:14057 (the official FR text). The batch scout's single end date (EO 14057, whole) would have misdated 28 of the 40 clauses, which is the earlier-partial-supersession lesson of Lambertini II (as with EO 10746 via EO 10900). A by-number scan (whitespace and hyphenation normalised) of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13834 named only in EO 13990 and EO 14057. EO 14148 (2025-01-20) later revoked EO 13990 but does not name EO 13834 and reinstates nothing, and EO 13834 had been revoked in full by EO 14057 more than three years earlier, so the 2025 revocation of EO 13990 revives no part of it. Reading record LSP-EO_14057 (EO 14057, 86 FR 70935-70943, read once in full): sec. 501 'reestablishe[s]' the Office of the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer within CEQ, sec. 502 has agencies designate Chief Sustainability Officers and secs. 504-508 reset the CEQ, OMB and agency duties and create working groups; sec. 604 revokes EO 13834 with no savings, transition or exception clause; the order mentions neither the Steering Committee nor any surviving provision of EO 13834, and its sec. 606(a) is a general non-impairment clause for agency authority. Reading record LSP-EO_13990 (reused, 86 FR 7037-7043): sec. 7(a) revoked EO 13834 on 2021-01-20 except secs. 6, 7 and 11; sec. 7(f) directs rescission of implementing measures. Own-residual check, reading EO 13834 in full: the one savings lead (the S3 prefill) is sec. 4(a), under which the Federal Interagency Sustainability Steering Committee 'shall continue in effect'; sec. 4 was among the sections revoked by EO 13990 on 2021-01-20, the Committee was a body continued by this order and not created by it, and EO 14057 does not mention it, so no continuing provision survives the revocation of the order. Sec. 6 (the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer and the Office of Federal Sustainability) is replaced by the re-established Office in EO 14057 sec. 501, which re-creates rather than preserves; sec. 8 revoked EO 13693, an executed revocation that nothing revives; the order created no right (sec. 11(c) disclaims rights), fund or property. EO 13868 (signed 2019-04-10, 84 FR 15495-15499), read in full from the held FR text, directs agency actions on energy infrastructure: Clean Water Act section 401 guidance and rules (sec. 3), LNG safety and rail-transport rules (sec. 4), a Labor Department review of ERISA data and proxy guidance (sec. 5), rights-of-way renewals (sec. 6), reports (secs. 7-9) and general provisions (sec. 10). The machine own-term kinds (condition, fixed_term, report_deadline, sunset_date) are all misleading: they pick up 60-, 100-, 120- and 180-day periods, '13 months' and '1 year' deadlines, and the word 'sunset' in sec. 6, which describes expiring rights-of-way grants issued by agencies, not an end of the order. None of these is an end and the order has no sunset or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. rationales.exact_text: Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13868 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13868 in full: it directs guidance, rulemakings, reviews and reports (Clean Water Act section 401, LNG rules, Labor review, rights-of-way renewals) and creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 10(c) disclaims rights). Rules and guidance issued by EPA, DOT and others under it were independent exercises of statutory authority; the order set up no continuing body, and sec. 6's rights-of-way renewals are agency grants, not rights of the order. EO 13875 (signed 2019-06-14, 84 FR 28711; read in full from the held Federal Register text) orders agencies to evaluate and terminate FACA advisory committees (sec. 1), caps eligible committees at 350 (sec. 2), sets reporting requirements (sec. 3), assigns OMB a role including waivers and recommendations (sec. 4), exempts merit review panels (sec. 5) and carries general provisions (sec. 6). Own-terms leads: the dossier's undated 'sunset_date' terms are the sec. 1(b) deadline 'by September 30, 2019' and the sec. 1(e) look-back; both are read in the clause reasons as performance deadlines and a counting window, not as ends of the order or of any clause, and its report_deadline terms (Aug. 1 and Sept. 1, 2019) are never ends. The limit of this reading: a command already performed may have been exhausted before 2021-01-20, which no held source dates, so the project rule 'a deadline is not an end' is followed and the revocation date is the first end of each clause. No amendment, suspension or extension of EO 13875 is found: the dossier lists no other-actor provision and no missing line, and the by-number scan finds EO 13875 named only in EO 13992 sec. 2. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The machine current-law searches found no hit for this order (no OLRC or eCFR mention); the OFR catalog edges are the revocation. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13875 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13875 is named only in EO 13992 sec. 2. Savings and the own-residual check are in savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13875 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agencies to rescind implementing orders, rules and policies and abolish entities established under the revoked orders 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'; sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause for statutory authority and OMB budget functions; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13875. Own-residual check, reading EO 13875 in full (secs. 1-6): it established no committee, office, fund or right; it required agencies to review and terminate FACA committees, cap the total at 350, report to OMB and let OMB recommend terminations. Committees an agency terminated under sec. 1(b) stay terminated, but each termination is an agency act under FACA authority and not an effect of the order that outlives it; EO 13992 sec. 3 has no entity of EO 13875 to abolish. The order has no implementing rule requirement. The prefill was S1 (transfer wording): the 'transfer' phrases belong to EO 13992 sec. 3 (rescission and abolition), which transfers nothing; kept as none_after_bounded_search after reading both orders. Bounded search: EO 13875 and EO 13992 in full; current-law usc/ecfr searches (no hit); the by-number scan.

EO 13891 (signed 2019-10-09, 84 FR 55235; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 38 clauses) sets the policy that guidance documents be non-binding (sec. 1), defines terms (sec. 2), requires agencies to publish a database of guidance documents and rescind unneeded ones (sec. 3), to finalize regulations on guidance-document procedures (sec. 4), applies EO 12866, 13563 and 13609 to guidance (sec. 5), tells OMB to implement (sec. 6) and has general provisions and carve-outs (sec. 7). Own-terms: the dossier flags 'fixed_term' leads (the '240 days' reinstatement window in sec. 3(b) and 'at least 30 days' of public comment in sec. 4(a)(iii)(A)), a 'report_deadline' (sec. 3(d)) and conditions. Read in the clause reasons: the 120/240/300-day periods run from the date of an OMB implementing memorandum that no held source dates, they are performance and reporting deadlines, the 240-day reinstatement permission narrows sec. 3(b) without ending it, and the 30-day period is a minimum comment requirement; none is an end of a clause or the order. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Dossier missing lines 'target provision not located: EO:12866, 13563, 13771, 13777, 1609': these orders predate EO 13891 (1993, 2011, 2017, 2017) and cannot amend it, and 'EO 1609 of May 1, 2012' in the OFR cross-reference is the mistyped number of EO 13609 (2012); EO 13891 only lists them as compliance standards. No order after EO 13891 other than EO 13992 names it in a held text. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note that EO 13891 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The three dossier machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13891 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13891 is named only in EO 13992 sec. 2 (other hits are Federal Register page numbers). Conflict, savings and the own-residual check are in conflict_resolutions and savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13891 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agency heads to rescind 'any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies ... implementing or enforcing' the revoked orders 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, including the Administrative Procedure Act', and, where rescission cannot be finalized immediately, to provide exemptions; sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13891. Own-residual check, reading EO 13891 in full (secs. 1-7): sec. 4(a) required each agency to 'finalize regulations, or amend existing regulations' setting out guidance-document processes within 300 days of OMB's memorandum, and sec. 6 had OMB issue memoranda and regulations. Regulations an agency finalized under sec. 4(a) are independent legal instruments that remain in force after the order is revoked until the agency rescinds them by notice and comment (the APA reference in EO 13992 sec. 3 says as much), so the order's implementing rules continue independently of it. The dossier's current-law leads (28 CFR part 813, 29 CFR part 1695, 45 CFR part 2509, 32 CFR part 339 and 49 CFR 5.39, which name EO 13891) are consistent with that reading but were not read as legal text (no held slice or sha256), so the state rests on the held texts of EO 13891 and EO 13992. The prefill was S4 (conflict): the conflict is resolved in conflict_resolutions and the savings state is continuing_independent, overruling the plain 'none' reading. Bounded search: EO 13891 and EO 13992 in full; the dossier's current-law leads and the three machine searches; the by-number scan.

partial change by EO 13924 sec. 5(a) (85 FR 31353, signed 2020-05-19; no effective-date wording, so effective on signing): heads of agencies other than the Department of Justice are to accelerate pre-enforcement rulings under EO 13892 about COVID-19 related conduct, and 'Pre-enforcement rulings under this subsection may be issued without regard to the requirements of section 6(a) of Executive Order 13892'. This relaxes the sec. 6(a) opportunity-to-be-heard requirement for that one class of rulings; it does not revoke or suspend sec. 6(a) for any other action and EO 13924 states no end of EO 13892, so it is a later event that narrows the clause and not a first end.

EO 13924 (signed May 19, 2020, 85 FR 31353-31356), read in full from the held official FR text, sets the policy of combating the economic consequences of COVID-19 by regulatory relief (sec. 1), defines terms by reference to EO 13892 (sec. 2), directs agency heads to use emergency authorities, to identify and rescind or waive regulatory standards, to speed pre-enforcement rulings and enforcement discretion, to apply fairness principles, to review their regulatory response and to report, and has OMB monitor (secs. 3-8), with general provisions (sec. 9). It has no term or sunset: it has no dated end, and the review and report in sec. 7 have no deadline except one OMB may set (sec. 8). EO 13927 (signed 2020-06-04, 85 FR 35165-35170), read in full from the held FR text, directs agencies to speed infrastructure and recovery actions during the COVID-19 national emergency: transportation, Army civil works and Federal-lands projects (secs. 3-5), NEPA, ESA and Clean Water Act emergency procedures (secs. 6-8), other emergency authorities (sec. 9) and general provisions (sec. 10). Most operative sections set a 30-day report and then status reports 'at least every 30 days for the duration of the national emergency'. The machine own-term kinds (condition, emergency_duration, fixed_term, report_deadline) are not ends: 30-day periods are deadlines, and the emergency-duration wording would end the recurring reports only when the emergency ended, which was after 2021-01-20 (no held source records an earlier end). The order has no sunset or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20; the U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 601 says the same (86 FR 7041). The dossier lists no missing provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13927 named only in EO 13990. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Such status reports shall thereafter be provided...'); inventory_overrides merge it into sec8-c. rationales.exact_text: Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13927 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. The recurring reports were continuing duties of the order, and the revocation ended them; nothing in EO 13990 keeps them running. EO 13979 (signed January 18, 2021, 86 FR 6813-6815), read in full from the held official FR text, requires agency heads to have section 553 rules signed, and the rulemaking process and regulatory agenda initiated or approved, only by senior appointees (sec. 2), to review and revise their delegations of rulemaking authority and amend agency management regulations within 180 days (sec. 3) and to review rules of the last 12 years and report within 120 days (sec. 4), with definitions, OIRA guidance and general provisions (secs. 5-7). EO 13986 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7015-7017), read in full from the held official FR text: sec. 1 background; sec. 2 apportionment policy; sec. 3 directs the Secretary of Commerce to report state population tabulations without regard to immigration status; sec. 4 data quality; sec. 5 revokes EO 13880 and the July 21, 2020 memorandum; sec. 6 general provisions. It has no term, sunset or termination wording; the own-term leads are statutory report timings (13 U.S.C. 141(b)-(c)) and the appropriations condition, none an end. EO 14148 sec. 2(b) (held text, 90 FR 8237-8241; reading record LSP-EO_14148) revokes EO 13986 by number with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, January 20, 2025; 2025-01-28 is only the FR printing date. Every clause therefore has first end 2025-01-20. The dossier's 11 clauses run contiguously from the enacting clause to sec. 6(c) (only line breaks, page furniture and the signature block lie between or after them), so the inventory is kept. D6: no held official text other than EO 14148 names EO 13986 and the OFR catalog records no amendment, so no later event changed any clause before the end. Conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW resolved (USC note is an editorial reprint). Savings: completed revocation of EO 13880 accrues.

Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (instruments/03/readings, text_sha256 65bf2d86... re-verified against the held jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14148.txt): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed actions with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20; sec. 3 directs agencies to end implementation and tells the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind actions taken under the listed orders; sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; no successor delegation, transfer of functions, funds or property, pending-matter clause, exception or revival wording. Own-residual check, reading EO 13986 in full (secs. 1-6): sec. 5 revoked EO 13880 (Collecting Information About Citizenship Status in Connection With the Decennial Census) and the Presidential Memorandum of July 21, 2020, on signing 2021-01-20. Revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked and EO 14148 has no revival wording, so EO 13880 stays revoked: an effect of EO 13986 survives it (accrued). Secs. 3-4 rest on the Secretary's statutory duties under 13 U.S.C. 141 and 2 U.S.C. 2a, which exist independently of the order; no function, fund or body was transferred; sec. 6(c) disclaims private rights. Bounded search: every held official FR text (jobs/fr-originals, EO 1 to EO 14435) was grepped for 13986 (only EO 14148 names it; the EO 9807 hit is a list number), OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv: only EO 13986 revoking EO 13880 and EO 14148 revoking EO 13986), the dossier current-law lead and the three machine searches.

Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 13988 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted.

Section 7(b) of Executive Order 14168 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8615) states that the requirements of that order supersede conflicting provisions in previous Executive Orders, including this order by number, and that "These Executive Orders are hereby rescinded". That is an express rescission of this order as a whole, with no effective-date wording, dated on signing, 2025-01-20. It is a second express rescission on the same day as Executive Order 14148 section 2 and gives no earlier date.

The order has no term, sunset or termination clause; the dossier's fixed_term and condition terms are the pledge periods, the sec. 5(b) sanction duration and the 'consistent with applicable law' clause, none of which ends a clause of the order before the revocation. EO 14148 sec. 2(e) revokes the whole order with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20. The dossier's missing line 'target provision not located: EO:14091' was read: EO 14091 sec. 2 (Agency Equity Teams) uses 'appointees, as defined in Executive Order 13989', a borrowed definition; it amends, extends or ends nothing in EO 13989, so it is ruled out as a later event, and EO 14091 was itself revoked by EO 14148 sec. 2(bbb). The dossier's 64-clause inventory is contiguous from sec. 1 through sec. 6(d) and was kept, except that the one-line list intro sec. 2(c) ('Gift':) was merged by override with its first item because the claim-checker cannot verify a quotation of fewer than 6 words and 30 characters (63 clauses); the pledge paragraphs sit inside clauses sec1 and sec1-c and are discussed there. The Code note at 5 U.S.C. 7301 note (MENTIONS.csv role eo_note_ended_status) states EO 13989 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, sec. 2(e), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8237', consistent with this ending (a machine-extracted lead, not relied on).

Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (official FR text 90 FR 8237, read once in full, text_sha256 65bf2d86... verified on disk): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed executive actions with no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording, so each revocation took effect on signing, 2025-01-20; sec. 3(b) directs the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind, replace or amend agency actions taken under the listed orders (it preserves no provision, office or right of any listed order); sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, no transfer of functions, funds or property, no pending-matter clause and no exception for any listed order. Own-residual check, reading EO 13989 in full (secs. 1-6): sec. 1 makes every appointee appointed on or after 2021-01-20 'contractually committed' to the pledge, pledge para. 9 incorporates the Order into the agreement as binding, and sec. 5(a) makes the commitments enforceable by the United States by debarment or civil proceedings. Pledges signed before 2025-01-20 are completed individual undertakings, some with periods that run 1 to 2 years or more after the signer's appointment or departure (paras. 2-6) plus a possible bar of up to 5 years under sec. 5(b). EO 14148 sec. 2(e) revokes the order without cancelling signed pledges, sec. 3 waivers or the pledge files kept under sec. 4(e), and revocation of an order does not by itself discharge obligations already assumed under it, so these accrued undertakings survive the order (accrued). How or whether they are enforced after the revocation is not decided by any held source, and the claim does not assert it. No function, fund or property was transferred or re-delegated by EO 13989 or EO 14148; the OGE, OMB and agency duties in sec. 4 rest on the order and end with it. Prefill was 'review' (S1_transfer_wording): decided from the reading and the order as transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: every held official FR text (EO 1 through EO 14435) was searched for the number 13989 and the title; only EO 14148 sec. 2(e) names it as a target, EO 14091 (revoked by EO 14148 sec. 2(bbb)) borrows its definition of 'appointees', and EO 13983 (2021) concerns EO 13770; OFR edges show only those; the three machine searches were read.
