Executive Order 8980 (official Federal Register text, 6 FR 6471, PDF pages 3-3, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits persons holding state, territorial or municipal office to accept appointment and serve as members of Alien Enemy Hearing Boards. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2's list ('include, but are not limited to') does not name it, but the order amends Executive Order No. 9 in terms and is therefore within section 2's general revocation; the 1989 OFR disposition table records 'Revoked by EO 11408' for it. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Alien Enemy Hearing Boards were wartime bodies convened by the Attorney General, but the permission names no particular board and no expiry, so it remained legally available (if unused) until revoked; no instrument ended it earlier. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

EO 9089 (Mar. 6, 1942; 7 FR 1777-1778) directs the Defense Communications Board to exercise the President's Communications Act sec. 606(d) powers over wire communication facilities (enacting words) under ten regulations parallel to EO 8964's radio regulations. Sec. 606(d), as quoted in the order, runs 'during the period ending not later than six months after the termination of such state or threat of war' or an earlier date set by concurrent resolution; the state of war had not been terminated by Feb. 24, 1947 and no such concurrent resolution is recorded in the bounded sources, so the statutory period had not run. EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board and amended this order accordingly. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 9089, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; every clause and the order first ended on 1947-02-24. 1989 Codification: 'Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'. No current-law citation. The draft's clause text quoted the footnote-joined number of EO 8546 (read as a non-existent order); the quotation is now split around it.

EO 9831 para. 1 abolishes the Board of War Communications and transfers all its property and records to the Federal Communications Commission; para. 2 revokes the five orders without any savings clause. The Board's records and property pass to the FCC; claims to just compensation for any government use or control of facilities rest on Communications Act sec. 606 itself, not on the revoked orders. No continuing effect rests on this order.

EO 9172 (May 22, 1942) created a National Railway Labor Panel 'for the duration of the war and six months thereafter' and let its chairman form three-member emergency boards (paras. 1-3; 7 FR 3913-3914, read in the held govinfo scan). Before taking the revocation as the first end I checked the order's own term: the state of war with Germany and Japan had not been terminated in August 1947 (the President's proclamation of December 31, 1946 ended only hostilities), so the Panel's own term had not run, and EO 9883's recital confirms the Panel still existed. No amendment or partial revocation is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification disposition table, a lead only). EO 9883 (12 FR 5481) revokes the order outright, states no effective date and has no savings clause, so every paragraph ended on its signing date, August 11, 1947. The U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches found no current citation.

EO 9883 is a bare revocation with no savings, transition or winding-up clause. EO 9172 itself contains none: it created the National Railway Labor Panel and its emergency boards, which existed only to investigate and report on disputes; reports already made were completed acts, and nothing in either order preserves pending board proceedings, pay or any right. Rail disputes reverted to the Railway Labor Act procedures that EO 9883's recital names as adequate.

EO 9213 (August 4, 1942, effective as of June 30, 1942) extended the committee for four years, from June 30, 1942 to June 30, 1946. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1946-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 9741 (June 25, 1946) extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1946 to June 30, 1950. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1950-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 9890 (September 6, 1947) restated the committee's authority to consult and advise named agencies and organizations, appointed Olaus J. Murie (printed 'Glaus' in the text layer) to a vacancy, and amended EO 6783 accordingly. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. The authority to consult and the amendment of EO 6783 had no term of their own and operated only while the committee existed, so they ceased with the committee on June 30, 1966. The appointment was a one-time act completed on issuance (if it were instead dated by the appointee's tenure, that tenure could not outlast the committee, so the whole-order end is unchanged). Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

Original section 3(e) would terminate the Council after two years. EO12783 expressly substitutes termination on January 16, 1993; that fixed termination command controls, rather than the original 1992 anniversary or the later 1993 formal revocation. No amendment effective date is inferred from its signing date. EO12869 expressly recognizes EO12720 as amended by EO12783 and revokes it effective September 30, 1993. The corrected nine-part inventory includes the original establishment, appointments, both advisory functions, information duty, compensation/travel, support/funding, FACA delegation, and sunset. The OCR joined section 3(d) into 3(c); exact disjoint original-source spans now separate them. The fixed sunset reaches the Council and its continuing institutional machinery; the later formal revocation reaches the entire order. Each information, funding, support, appointment, and FACA instruction is expressly for this Council or its functions. None directs a separate post-Council program. The appropriation qualifier is not a cessation event. Travel rights for work already performed are accounted for as accrued effects rather than a continuing council mandate. No express prospective saving appears in EO12783 or EO12869 for this Council. Section 3(b) nevertheless permits accrued statutory travel expenses, so the residual classification preserves possible accrued rights without asserting that any particular unpaid claim exists. USC119-121 is only current through2026-10-09 and is not asserted as a complete cutoff predicate. No human approval or publication is asserted.

Advising the AID Administrator, reporting progress to the Deputy Secretary, services, travel, procurement and FACA delegation are separately inventoried. Reporting to the Deputy Secretary is a function and supplies no automatic report-completion termination. The packet does not supply an actual termination/closeout record. Original section 4(b) says the Commission shall terminate not later than September 30, 1992. EO12815 replaces only the date with December 31, 1992. This is a termination limit, unlike a report deadline, but the retained not-later-than wording and EO12869 description of committees terminated or work completed do not uniquely establish the actual first cessation date. I decline to convert that limit into an exact historical event.

Treasury delegation, agency measures, emergency declaration and blocking are separately considered from import/export/travel/transport and other prohibitions. Completed transfers under EO12817 cannot by themselves establish a whole-order end. No Treasury determination, exhaustion, or signing-date effective event is inferred. EO12724 section 6 revokes EO12722 only to the extent inconsistent and continues administrative acts under the new order. EO12771 expressly does not terminate the Iraq emergency. EO12817 creates specific transfer mechanisms. EO13303 section 2(a) removes the orders from selected property, with section 2(b) savings. EO13350 revokes EO12722 but preserves blocked-property prohibitions and accrued effects. These are distinct partial transitions and cannot be replaced by one July30,2004 first-end date.

The military department discretion is part of the single construction authority. Immediate commencement and transmission/publication implement that invocation and do not create separate continuing construction authority after emergency termination. No performance or congressional transmission date is asserted. The original makes the 10 USC2808 invocation available immediately under the EO12722 Iraq emergency. EO12722 and EO12724 precede EO12734, so missing machine target provisions for those actors cannot establish a later cessation of this order. EO12771 expressly leaves the Iraq emergency unaffected. EO13303 addresses selected property, and EO12817 transfer authority, rather than construction authority. No earlier cessation is identified in the held chain or selected bounded later-order search.

Complete operative source spans selected by independent comparison with the held original. The original has one operative construction invocation plus effective/publication implementation. It invokes 10 USC2808 according to its terms, for Defense and military department Secretaries, and contains no finite project, report, fixed expiration, or separate independent program. EO13350 explicitly revokes EO12734 and terminates its underlying emergency; section 10 makes that action effective July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT, not July 29 signing.

Treasury action, compelled bank transfers, Federal Reserve receiving/holding/investing/transferring, implementation, definitions, noncreation of enforceable rights and immediate/publication instructions were each considered. None supplies prospective independent transfer authority after express revocation. Section 4 protects qualifying historical conduct; its accrued effects are separately preserved. No actual administrative completion or congressional transmission event is inferred. Sections 1-3 establish continuing Treasury, bank-transfer and Federal Reserve authority with conditional transfers; an actual transfer does not exhaust the authority to address other assets or repayments. Neither an assumed transfer date nor UNSCR778 adoption is used as an end. The held chain identifies EO13350 as the express revocation, effective under its section 10 on July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT.

EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.

EO 10192 (December 15, 1950, 15 FR 9029) was read in the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10192.txt, 19,424 chars). The order is only the two numbered amendments at about chars 15,127-15,308; the rest of the extract is neighbouring Federal Register material including EO 10193. It amends EO 10129 of June 3, 1950 (President's Commission on Migratory Labor, held): para 1 changes the paragraph 3 report date from 'December 15, 1950' to 'March 1, 1951'; para 2 changes 'Thirty days' to 'Sixty days' in paragraph 8 (EO 10129 para 8 as issued: 'Thirty days after rendition of its report to the President, the Commission shall cease to exist unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order'). The first end is EO 10236 (signed 1951-04-26, 16 FR 3607; held official text): 'paragraph 8 ... as amended by paragraph 2 of Executive Order No. 10192 ... be, and it is hereby, further amended to read as follows: "8. The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951."' Clause 2 (the 'Sixty days' wording) was replaced on 1951-04-26; clause 1 (the changed report date) was spent when the Commission ceased to exist at the end of 1951-05-31, which is also the whole-order end. A report deadline is not an end and the actual report date is not held, so I treated the amendment of a deadline as ending with the body whose report it governed; the independent reviewer should test that choice. The machine searches (usc 0 hits, ecfr 0 hits, OFR catalog 1 hit) carry no coverage warning; the single catalog hit points at EO 10263 only because of a mis-attributed date and is resolved above.

EO 10999 (Assigning Emergency Preparedness Functions to the Secretary of Commerce, signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1527-1532) was read in full from the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10999.txt, 24,413 chars; page images not inspected). The extract begins with the tail of EO 10998 (Agriculture, Secs. 8-12) and ends with the opening of EO 11000 (Labor); neither is part of EO 10999. The machine draft inventory had 46 records with duplicated sub-items that mixed those neighbours, so I replaced it with the 13 sections of EO 10999 (Secs. 1-13) using absolute character spans in the held file. EO 10999 has no sunset. Its first end is EO 11490 (signed 1969-10-28, 34 FR 17567): Sec. 3015 'The following are hereby revoked:' lists '(7) Executive Order No. 10999 of February 16, 1962' (official Federal Register text jobs/family-rule-tail/output/texts/EO_11490_tail.txt, and the APP transcription); the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note independently records that EO 10999 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11490, Oct. 28, 1969, 34 F.R. 17567'. EO 11490 states no effective date or delay, so it took effect on signing, 1969-10-28. Sec. 3014 (retention of existing authority) is expressly 'except as provided by Section 3015' and so does not save EO 10999. Search scope: current-law:usc (one editorial note stating the revocation), current-law:ecfr (no section in the eCFR search hits lists EO 10999), later-events:ofr_catalog (all hits are EO 11490); none has a coverage warning. The dossier's missing item (EO 10952, a Department of Defense order named in Sec. 6) is only a cross-reference and is not an acting instrument for EO 10999.

Service performed and pay earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects. Own-terms end on the stated 'until' date. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling the end is recorded as that date, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the stated alternative. The date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline on some other act. No held record shows the employee's death or separation before that date; if such a record is found, the claim must be reopened to decide whether the exemption lapsed earlier. No held order amends, revokes or shortens this order.

The complete original page confirms one designation covering thirteen agencies under EO 7916 section 6. The complete EO 9830 and official pages 1, 3, 4 and 11 confirm express whole-order revocation effective May 1, 1947 and no target-specific saving. Primary EO 7916 pages 8–9 show a February 1, 1939 implementation bound followed by continuing director duties, so initial establishment does not exhaust the designation. Actual EO 8044 limits competitive coverage; actual EO 8363 changes parent section 3 and EO 8467 changes section 7. None changes section 6 or names EO 7975-A. Wrong adjacent instrument attributions in the prior review were corrected from original pages. No earlier end was found in the stated bounded searches and primary checks. Exact sources and limitations appear in ANALYSIS.md and SUPPLEMENT_RECEIPT.json.

The original contains no savings. The complete EO 9830 has no reservation of the target designation. Section 01.3 independently requires personnel offices; section 01.5 expressly continues and renames the Council of Personnel Administration. That separate institutional continuation is disclosed, rather than treated as continuation of the revoked thirteen-agency designation. No target-specific accrued or transferred right was found in these complete texts.

The complete primary EO 7916, PDF pages 8–9, printed pages 1526–1527, makes establishment effective not later than February 1, 1939 and assigns continuing liaison, budget, supervision, training, grievance and Council duties. That implementation bound is not a sunset; no actual completion date is inferred. Actual EO 8043 amends Schedules A/B. Actual EO 8044 suspends only the competitive-coverage function. Actual EO 8363, rather than neighboring 8364, modifies parent section 3. Actual EO 8467, rather than neighboring 8468, restates section 7 effective July 1, 1940 while retaining personnel directors as ex officio Council members. Relevant complete personnel provisions and original pages were read. No earlier first end was found within the disclosed bounds. Own-terms expiry on the stated date, recorded per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling as the stated date inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading (the exemption ends when that day begins) is one day earlier and is stated here for the human reviewer. No later order amends, revokes or extends this order before its stated date (see the search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act.

Own-terms expiry on the stated date, recorded per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling as the stated date inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading (the exemption ends when that day begins) is one day earlier and is stated here for the human reviewer. The person's death, resignation or separation before the stated date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an earlier termination of the order; no held record shows any such event. A later 'further exemption' of the same person signed before this order's stated date is a new, overlapping grant that neither revokes nor shortens this order's term (it recites this order and adds a later end date), so it is recorded as a later event, not as an earlier ending. No later order amends, revokes or extends this order before its stated date (see the search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act.
